papers.title: CLEAR: Prototype-conditioned flow purification for LLM-based rumor detection with Dirichlet evidential learning
papers.authors: Liu Z., Wu H., Fang X., Liu G., Li H., Jing Z., Zhang H.
papers.abstract: Detecting rumors on social media is challenging when posts are semantically underspecified and discussion threads are noisy or polarized, which can encourage detectors to exploit spurious correlations. We propose CLEAR (Contextual Potential Alignment Capture Network), an evidence-grounded framework that models hierarchical comment dynamics and incorporates auxiliary LLM-based veracity assessments for credibility-aware prediction. CLEAR couples prototype-conditioned flow purification with Dirichlet evidential learning to derive geometry-grounded evidence for calibrated inference. We further introduce an entropy-adaptive Hard-Shift reweighting strategy to suppress noise-driven shortcuts. Experiments on Weibo-19 (2927 samples) and PHEME (2018 samples) show that CLEAR achieves 93.16% and 91.56% accuracy, outperforming the average strong recent baselines by 3.2 and 5.5 percentage points, respectively. To stress-test generalization under distribution shift, we curate VRDD with 4020 posts (2348 non-rumors and 1672 rumors), a boundary-dense benchmark that emphasizes vague content. Results confirm CLEAR’s robustness to evolving rumor patterns and highlight the curriculum-dependent effect of reweighting.

papers.title: Toward accurate and cost-effective LLM agents via information flow optimization: Insights from a phishing detection case study
papers.authors: Trad F., Chehab A.
papers.abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated strong performance on complex decision-making tasks that require reasoning over heterogeneous inputs. However, these gains often come at a substantial operational cost, as incorporating additional modalities and tool calls leads to rapidly increasing API usage in real-world deployments. We argue that this tension is not solely a modeling issue, but a consequence of how information is shared with agents, and we systematically investigate how information-flow design shapes the performance–cost trade-off in LLM-based agentic systems. Using phishing website detection as a representative case study, we evaluate a spectrum of LLM-based agent designs spanning single-input baselines, parallel-input agents, and progressively more cost-aware sequential strategies. While providing all information in parallel improves detection performance, it incurs prohibitive costs due to large input sizes. To address this, we examine sequential escalation strategies that defer expensive inputs until earlier evidence proves insufficient. A multi-agent pipeline following a fixed, cost-aware sequence reduces cost substantially while maintaining competitive accuracy. Building on this, a single-agent sequential design that preserves reasoning context across steps further improves performance (F1-score = 0.964) with only a moderate cost increase. Finally, a dynamic sequential agent that autonomously selects which information to request next achieves the highest performance (F1-score = 0.974), though at higher operational cost. These results demonstrate that structured information flow, not merely model choice, plays an important role in determining the accuracy–cost trade-offs of agentic AI systems. While our findings are based on phishing detection as a representative case study, extending these insights across domains remains an important direction for future work.

papers.title: Memory-KGC: Memory-augmented structural learning for Knowledge Graph Completion
papers.authors: Li J., Sun Y., Xu B., Pan D., Luo L., Lin H.
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs), Knowledge Graphs (KGs) have become crucial for enhancing factual reasoning in Natural Language Processing (NLP). However, the inherent incompleteness of KGs limits their effectiveness, motivating the Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) task, which aims to infer missing relations from known facts. Existing KGC approaches often rely on local subgraphs, which restrict global structural utilization and may introduce noise. To address these limitations, we propose Memory-KGC, a memory-augmented structural learning framework for KGC. Our model introduces a trainable memory module that explicitly captures and stores the global structural knowledge of KGs, while integrating local subgraph information to refine entity matching and reduce noise. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets, including large-scale graphs with over 4.5 million entities, show that Memory-KGC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of both the memory module and subgraph integration.

papers.title: FedCRF: A Federated Cross-domain Recommendation method with semantic-driven deep knowledge Fusion
papers.authors: Guo L., Yang T., Yu X., Han X., Jiang G., Liu H.
papers.abstract: As user behavior data becomes increasingly scattered across different platforms, achieving cross-domain knowledge fusion while preserving privacy has become a critical issue in recommender systems. Existing Privacy-Preserving Cross-Domain Recommendation (PPCDR) methods usually rely on overlapping users or items as a bridge, making them inapplicable to non-overlapping scenarios. They also suffer from limitations in the collaborative modeling of global and local semantics. To this end, this paper proposes a Federated Cross-domain Recommendation method with deep knowledge Fusion (FedCRF). Using textual semantics as the cross-domain bridge, FedCRF achieves cross-domain knowledge transfer via federated semantic learning under the non-overlapping scenario. Specifically, FedCRF constructs global semantic clusters on the server side to extract shared semantic information, and designs a Fine-Grained Semantic Adaptation and Transfer (FGSAT) module on the client side to dynamically adapt to local data distributions and alleviate cross-domain distribution shift. Meanwhile, it builds a semantic graph based on textual features to learn representations that integrate both structural and semantic information, and introduces contrastive learning constraints between global and local semantic representations to enhance semantic consistency and promote deep knowledge fusion. In this framework, only item semantic representations are shared, while user interaction data remains locally stored, effectively mitigating privacy leakage risks. Experimental results on multiple real-world datasets show that FedCRF significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of Recall@20 and NDCG@20, validating its effectiveness and superiority in non-overlapping cross-domain recommendation scenarios.

papers.title: Veritas: Structuring and verifying LLM knowledge for logically consistent behavior tree generation in LLM-based agents
papers.authors: Tang H., Zhang F., Wan K., Lu S., Zhang X., Yao Y., Xu X.
papers.abstract: Behavior trees (BTs) have been widely adopted in autonomous task planning because of their modularity and reactivity. Recently, automatic BT generation based on Large Language Models (LLMs) has attracted growing research attention. However, synthesizing BTs for long-horizon tasks without relying on predefined expert rules remains an open problem, and it poses two key challenges: ensuring the logical consistency of the generated BTs, and maintaining their factual alignment with the ground truth of the environment. To address these challenges, this paper presents Veritas, a novel verification-driven framework for automatically generating logically consistent BTs. Veritas integrates STRIPS-like symbolic operators with a multi-layered verification mechanism, thereby transforming the planning process into a coherent chain of logical derivations. We further introduce Veritas+, which augments this framework with a memory module that accumulates both successful and failed execution experiences, enabling dynamic self-correction and improving factual consistency. We evaluate the framework on 67 long-horizon tasks in Minecraft and 116 real-world tasks in AndroidWorld. Experimental results show that Veritas and Veritas+ are highly effective and significantly outperform state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Data ethics in training large language models: A systematic review of machine-learning strategies and AI governance frameworks
papers.authors: Aldehim G., Shah S.F.A., Khan M.A., Mazhar T., Ahmad W., Saudagar A.K.J., Shahid M., Hamam H.
papers.abstract: We conduct a systematic review of ethical, technical, and governance challenges in the development and deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) and map these challenges to machine-learning (ML) strategies and governance practices reported in recent research. Using a PRISMA-guided process, we identified 1300 records, removed 220 duplicates (1080 unique), screened titles/abstracts, assessed 480 full texts, and included 101 studies (2021–2025) spanning healthcare, education, law, and public policy. From this corpus, we synthesize a taxonomy covering data curation, consent and privacy, bias representation, provenance, and auditability, and align each area with actionable ML controls (e.g., documentation and tracing, bias detection and mitigation, privacy-preserving learning, quality checks, and auditing). Building on this synthesis, we present an integrative governance framework that links dataset processes and ML controls to oversight checkpoints across the LLM lifecycle, supporting accountable development and deployment. Overall, the review provides an evidence-based map from ethical risks to implementable ML techniques and governance touchpoints to reduce harm and strengthen transparency and accountability in real-world LLM pipelines.

papers.title: EvoJail: Evolutionary diverse jailbreak prompt generation for large language models
papers.authors: Tang R., Xu K., Cheng P., Ren H., Wang H., Jiang S.
papers.abstract: As LLMs continue to shape real-world applications, automated jailbreak generation becomes essential to reveal safety weaknesses and guide model improvement. Existing automatic jailbreak generation methods have not yet fully considered two important aspects: adaptability to evolving safety-finetuned models, which affects their effectiveness on newer model versions, and diversity in generated prompts, which can cause narrow or repetitive attack patterns. To address these issues, we propose EvoJail, an instruction-fusion-driven evolutionary jailbreak generation framework that formalizes jailbreak prompt generation as a multi-objective black-box optimization problem and leverages the principles of evolutionary algorithms to search for jailbreak prompts that can adapt across different model versions and exhibit diverse attack patterns. Specifically, EvoJail integrates jailbreak prompt generation into an iterative evolutionary loop, where at each iteration candidate prompts are evaluated directly against the target model and then selected and varied based on the target model’s responses, enabling the generation process to continuously adapt to model updates. To enhance diversity, EvoJail introduces field-aware instruction fusion to construct diverse starting points and incorporates diversity-aware objectives into the evolutionary fitness function, guiding the search toward prompts with richer semantic variation, while further designing multi-level LLM-based mutation operators that modify prompt structures at different granularities to promote structural diversity throughout the evolutionary process. The performance of EvoJail has been evaluated using five widely-used LLMs from the perspectives of effectiveness, adaptability, diversity, and efficiency. Results demonstrate that EvoJail has stronger adaptability and can achieve over 93% attack success rate and more than 5.6% improvement in diversity metrics over state-of-the-art methods. Source code is released at https://github.com/kaikaikai7/EvoJail.

papers.title: Leveraging GraphSAGE and large language models with cross-attention for transaction fraud detection: Evidence from credit card and PaySim datasets
papers.authors: Mohawesh R., Maqsood S., Salameh H.B., Elrefae G.
papers.abstract: Online purchasing fraud has grown with e-commerce, causing economic losses and undermining consumer trust. Due to its diversity and dynamism, few studies have examined e-commerce fraud detection. Traditional machine learning algorithms, such as random forest and support vector machines, have achieved poor performance because they do not always capture the rich contextual metadata or the underlying relational structure between transactions. In response to these shortcomings, we introduce a new hybrid fraud detection method that utilizes a lightweight large language model (specifically, DistilBERT) and Graph Neural Networks (GraphSAGE). Using a cross-attention mechanism, our model learns both structural information encoded in the transaction network and semantic information (e.g., transaction type and metadata). By including rich metadata embeddings and transaction graph structures into its architecture, the model learns to effectively detect frauds, even when signals are weak or unclear. With this connection, fraud detection becomes more efficient and resilient. Two benchmark datasets were used for the experiments: the PaySim financial transaction simulator and the European Credit Card Dataset (ECCD). The suggested model obtained 89.1% accuracy, 85.0% F1-score, and 85.5% AUC on ECCD and 90.0% accuracy, 87.0% F1-score, and 85.0% AUC on PaySim using a chronological 70/10/20 train-validation-test split. These findings show that, in comparison to single-modality models, merging structural transaction graphs with semantic metadata greatly enhances fraud detection performance.

papers.title: A self-guided few-shot semantic segmentation model based on query foreground-background similarity
papers.authors: Hong J., Hu H., Chen X., Ai K., Zhou Q., Zhang X.
papers.abstract: AbstractFew-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) commonly relies on generic support query matching. However, existing methods generally overlook two key cues: (i) Humans discriminate new categories by focusing on distinct image regions (e.g., salient foreground vs. background), but current methods lack such selective attention modeling. (ii) Pixels within a single object show much stronger feature consistency than pixels across different instances of the same class, even with intra-object variation. Based on this observation, we proposed SGTNet, which instead uses a Self-Guided Transformer (SGT) to refine the query itself. Specifically, SGT utilizes intra-query feature similarity to partition query images into distinguishable and ambiguous regions, dynamically guiding interactions between them to enhance discriminative capabilities. Extensive experiments on mainstream FSS benchmarks and cross-domain evaluation settings demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods. Additional analyses validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed token partitioning and interaction strategy. The implementation code has been made publicly accessible at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SGTNet-BF5E

papers.title: Community detection in multiplex networks via multiview layer-specific graphformers-based embedding with heuristic weighting and refinement strategies
papers.authors: Bouyer A., Arasteh B., Liu X., Sefati S.S., Kusetogullari H.
papers.abstract: Community detection in multiplex networks is a challenging task due to heterogeneous layer structures, weak inter-layer consistency, and noisy relations. The main objective of this study is to design an effective community detection framework that can adaptively exploit layer-specific information while preserving meaningful global structures across layers. To address this problem, we propose a new method named MLGFA, which integrates multiview layer-specific GraphFormers-based embeddings with heuristic layer weighting and label refinement strategies. The method first obtains expressive node embeddings for each layer, capturing both local and semi-local structural patterns. Then, an adaptive layer weighting mechanism is applied to quantify the relative contribution of each layer during node similarity computation. Finally, a deep learning-based boundary node reassignment process is employed to refine ambiguous community labels. The proposed framework by combining heuristic initialization, transformer-based representation, adaptive layer weighting, and deep filtering of the detected communities provides an efficient approach for identifying community structures in multiplex networks. The proposed framework is evaluated on several real-world and synthetic multiplex networks generated using the LFR benchmark. Experimental results are compared against several state-of-the-art methods, including GenLouvain, Infomap, MDLPA, LCDMN, MVGL, MPBTV, DGFM3, and LART. The results show that MLGFA consistently achieves higher or competitive performance in terms of NMI and ARI, especially under high mixing parameters. For example, obtained results on multiple real-world and synthetic multiplex datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over the best competing baseline methods, with relative NMI gains ranging from 0.26% to 122.81% across real networks and from 9.23% to 22.04% on LFR benchmarks. This indicates the high capability of MLGFA in extracting the structure of real communities in multiplex networks. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/phdutm2009/Multiplex-Community-Detection.

papers.title: L-SIMCL: label-guided semantic interaction with multi-dimensional contrastive learning for hierarchical text classification
papers.authors: Xu W., Zhang S., Yuan C.
papers.abstract: Hierarchical text classification (HTC) remains challenging under complex label hierarchies and long-tailed distributions. Current HTC models typically rely on static label dependency modeling and implicit regularization to integrate hierarchical information, which leads to the inability to dynamically capture fine-grained semantic information based on labels and difficulty in constructing discriminative boundaries for long-tailed labels in the embedding space. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Label-guided Semantic Interaction with Multi-dimensional Contrastive Learning model (L-SIMCL). First, a new label-guided semantic interaction module is proposed, which employs multi-head attention mechanisms to generate a unique, context-aware embedding for each label. Second, a new hierarchical hard negative construction method is proposed, which leverages parent-child and sibling relationships in the label hierarchy to construct hard negative samples at the sample-level. Third, a new hierarchical distance-aware optimization method is proposed, which leverages the label hierarchy to adaptively modulate the embedding distance between labels at the label-level. The efficacy of L-SIMCL was evaluated using four real-world HTC datasets: WOS, RCV1-V2, NYT and BGC. On the more hierarchically complex NYT dataset, L-SIMCL outperforms the strongest contrastive learning-based baseline, achieving absolute gains of 0.15% in Micro-F1 and 0.28% in Macro-F1, while demonstrating competitive performance on the RCV1-V2 dataset. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of L-SIMCL, particularly in addressing the challenges of complex label hierarchies and long-tailed distributions.

papers.title: PsychoDial: A framework for building a suicide risk dialogue dataset in human-AI conversations
papers.authors: Chen X., Li Q., Jiang Y., Liu M., Yang L., Jing X., Wei Z., Cao L.
papers.abstract: Suicide has a serious impact on families and society. As more people start to share their feelings with AI, human-AI dialogues present new opportunities for suicide risk detection. However, this field faces two major hurdles: (1) it lacks dedicated datasets, and (2) existing detection models, which are trained on social media, perform poorly in the unique context of human-AI interaction. This study’s goal is to fill these gaps by (1) constructing the first high-quality, scenario-specific dataset and (2) developing effective cross-scenario detection models. For the dataset, we develop the PsychoDial Framework, a novel method grounded in real user data and psychological theory. Using this framework, we generate 4040 multi-turn dialogues, including 2000 risk dialogues and 2040 non-risk dialogues. This dataset is rigorously validated, achieving high quality scores from human experts (9.28/10) and LLMs (9.32/10). For detection, our proposed LLM-based cross-scenario methods learn common expressive patterns across social media and new Human-AI dialogue situation. Our methods surpass all single-scenario baselines, achieving accuracy scores of 0.92 and 0.84 in the respective scenarios. By constructing the first high-quality dataset and proposing the cross-scenario baseline models, this work greatly promotes future research for the critical task of suicide risk detection in human-AI interactions. papers.title: Which LLM performs best in crisis knowledge generation? Automatic evaluation across multiple events and knowledge categories
papers.authors: Han R., An L., Zhou W., Chen M., Li G.
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) offer the possibility of automatically generating crisis knowledge. However, the content they generate must meet the strict requirements of high accuracy and actionability. Existing general evaluation methods and benchmarks struggle to assess these aspects effectively. To address this, this study constructs CKEval, an automated evaluation benchmark for crisis knowledge generation. This dataset covers four types of public emergencies and four categories of knowledge: conceptual, factual, rule-based, and model-based. It contains over 500,000 entries. Based on the multidimensional knowledge quality theory, we design an indicator system with five dimensions: intrinsic quality, contextual quality, representational quality, actionable quality, and effectiveness quality. We also innovatively propose a dual-path automatic scoring framework. This framework combines rule-based objective computation with LLM-based intelligent evaluation. Eight mainstream models are systematically evaluated using this benchmark. The results show that models like Claude and GPT lead in overall performance. All models excel in basic dimensions such as security and neutrality. However, they show significant weaknesses in completeness, interpretability, and user adaptability, which directly impact practical usability. The benchmark and framework developed in this study provide a scientific basis and practical tool for evaluating, comparing, and optimizing LLMs in the field of crisis management.

papers.title: FFC: Clustering via identification of edge objects based on feature-force
papers.authors: Han S., Li J., Liu X., Xue J., Qu J.
papers.abstract: Traditional clustering methods often suffer from a critical issue that cluster performance heavily relies on centroids or core-region samples. Inappropriate core-point assignment can lead to catastrophic consequences in cluster partitioning. To address this issue, we propose a novel Feature Force-based Clustering (FFC) method, introducing an edge-prioritized paradigm to reduce dependency on core regions. FFC introduces the Feature Force (FF) metric to identify edge-region samples, a Subcluster Formation and Merger Strategy (SFMS) for boundary clustering, and a set-distance metric for core-region assignment. Empirical experiments on 11 synthetic/real-world datasets (e.g., Circle, Moon, Olivetti Faces) demonstrate FFC achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance, with perfect clustering (ARI=1.000) on non-convex Moon/Circle datasets and 20.4% higher ARI than Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) on overlapping Aggregation data. Its edge-first mechanism effectively mitigates core-region dependency, while enabling accurate identification of arbitrary cluster shapes and edge structures. FFC also offers a transformative paradigm for clustering task by breaking traditional centroid/core reliance through the novel FF-based edge-first assignment strategy, and opens new research frontiers at the intersection of clustering and edge detection methodologies with nature-inspired concept (FF). The code of FFC will be available at https://github.com/Hankbet/FFC.

papers.title: Unified Generative Intent Discovery: Bridging in-domain classification and open-world intent generation
papers.authors: Zhao X., Liu Y., Huang Y., Liao Y., Tian L., Zhou B.
papers.abstract: Open-world intent discovery is critical for task-oriented dialogue systems, where static intent taxonomies fail to capture emerging user intentions and existing methods show limited generalization beyond predefined label spaces. To address this issue, we propose Unified Generative Intent Discovery (UGID), a unified framework that reformulates intent understanding as a conditional text generation task, enabling both in-domain (IND) intent classification and out-of-domain (OOD) intent discovery within a single architecture. UGID adopts a two-stage training strategy. First, instruction-tuned supervised fine-tuning strengthens semantic discrimination among known intents. Second, a self-play reinforcement learning mechanism simulates iterative user–system interactions to explore, refine, and validate novel intent labels. In addition, a reward design combining semantic fidelity and domain relevance guides the generation process toward coherent and meaningful intent discovery. Experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that UGID consistently achieves strong performance, reaching ACC scores of 79.63%, 82.70% and 87.50% on BANKING, StackOverflow and CLINC, respectively. Compared with the strongest generative baseline, IntentGPT-4, UGID further improves ACC by 14.87 and 4.21 percentage points on BANKING and CLINC, respectively. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of the proposed design. Overall, UGID provides an effective and scalable framework for intent understanding in dynamic open-world dialogue scenarios.

papers.title: KG-LTSR: Knowledge graph-augmented contrastive learning for sequential recommendation of long-tail users
papers.authors: Zhang Z., Wang M., Ji S., Li J., Zhang Y., Ren Y., Deng Q.
papers.abstract: Long-tail users pose persistent challenges for sequential recommendation due to their extremely short interaction sequences. While existing sequential recommendation approaches that leverage knowledge graph (KG) or data augmentation attempt to address this problem, they often introduce semantic noise or fail to meaningfully enrich the inherently limited interaction sequences. To this end, we propose KG-LTSR, a KG-augmented contrastive learning approach that strategically enhances sequential recommendation for long-tail users. KG-LTSR first performs a semantic-aware similar item selection process on a collaborative KG to filter out irrelevant relations and identify semantically similar candidate items. Leveraging these candidates, we then design two KG-driven sequence augmentation operators (i.e., KG-Replace and KG-Insert) that preserve sequence integrity while enriching short sequences with similar items. These operators are integrated into a contrastive learning paradigm to generate robust self-supervised views. Through multi-task training, KG-LTSR jointly optimizes the primary recommendation task, contrastive self-supervision learning, and KG embedding through parameters sharing. This ensures that KG-LTSR learns high-quality representations for long-tail users’ sequences. Extensive experiments conducted on four real-world datasets demonstrate that KG-LTSR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in sequential recommendation for long-tail users, achieving average improvements of 5.87% in HR and 6.69% in NDCG. The code is available at: https://github.com/ZZP-RS/KG-LTSR.

papers.title: Adaptive online bagging with hybrid sampling for non-stationary imbalanced data streams: A case study on credit card fraud detection
papers.authors: Yin H., Teng Y., Zhang X., Yu L.
papers.abstract: Detecting credit card fraud in streaming data demands simultaneous adaptation to class imbalance and concept drift—two challenges that degrade model performance. A unified Adaptive Online Bagging with Hybrid Sampling (AOBHS) framework is designed to address both challenges in streaming fraud detection. AOBHS employs a drift-sensitive sketch estimator to guide hybrid sampling of underrepresented fraudulent cases, generating temporally relevant minority samples to preserve class balance amid concept drifts. Furthermore, by combining active drift detection with passive performance-based replacement of underperforming classifiers, AOBHS adopts a dual-mode drift adaptation strategy that addresses both abrupt and gradual drifts, enhancing fraud identification accuracy over time. Comprehensive empirical evaluations across 108 synthetic datasets with 9 drift types, 5 real-world datasets across multiple domains, and a credit card transactions case study, demonstrate that AOBHS maintains robust and competitive performance compared to established benchmarks, with particular strengths in Recall, G-mean, and operational cost. These results confirm that AOBHS is particularly suited for scenarios where high recall and low operational cost are critical, and reveal its practical value for strengthening financial risk management and operational resilience in digital payment systems.

papers.title: Synthetic dataset generation for theft event extraction in Italian
papers.authors: Bonisoli G., Rollo F., Po L.
papers.abstract: Event extraction is the task of automatically identifying and extracting structured information about events from unstructured text. Despite Italian being a well-resourced language, it still lacks annotated datasets specifically designed for fine-grained event extraction. To address this gap, we propose a novel methodology for the generation of synthetic data suitable for fine-grained event extraction tasks. This work is motivated by the high cost and limited scalability of manual annotation. We introduce a controlled synthetic data generation pipeline that strictly adheres to a target annotation schema, providing a scalable alternative to extensive human labeling. The key methodological innovation is a two-phase, document-level generation framework that leverages Large Language Models, ensures structural consistency and mitigates generation biases, enabling the creation of high-quality datasets for complex event extraction scenarios. Using this methodology, we release SYNTH-ITA, the first collection of four medium-scale synthetic datasets for fine-grained Italian event extraction, generated from 10,000 structured crime scenarios each. Experiments conducted on event argument extraction using a QA formulation demonstrate that fine-tuning models on SYNTH-ITA leads to better or comparable performances to models fine-tuned on 200 manually annotated real news articles (+14% improvement with ELECTRA, -0.4% with BERT). Conversely, NER-based models for event argument extraction trained on synthetic data exhibit an 18% performance drop compared to those trained on manually annotated articles.

papers.title: Knowledge graphs and large language models for prompt-based scientometric inquiry
papers.authors: Correia A., Saarela M., Kärkkäinen T.
papers.abstract: Scientometrics is undergoing a methodological transformation driven by the increasing availability of large-scale scientific data and advances in artificial intelligence (AI). Traditional approaches centered on citation analysis and bibliographic coupling are now complemented by methods that leverage semantic representations, structured knowledge, and natural language understanding. However, current generative AI systems pose inherent challenges such as hallucinations, lack of transparency in decision-making and explainability, and issues with source reliability. In this article, we seek to mitigate these challenges by outlining a framework that integrates knowledge graphs (KGs) and large language models (LLMs) for scientometric inquiry. Taking a socio-technical perspective, the article sets out to explore the intersectional space of computing and information science from a human-centered approach. The framework is designed to support both established scientometric tasks, such as trend analysis, topic detection, and collaboration mapping, and more exploratory, insight-generating applications, including question answering, knowledge discovery, and contextual enrichment of scientific content. Drawing on recent developments in the use of KGs and LLMs in scientific domains, we provide a comparative overview of existing work, identify key design principles, and discuss the advantages and limitations of such a framework. Our goal is to chart a pathway toward more interactive, transparent, and generative approaches in information science and cross-disciplinary research.

papers.title: ERA: Aligning semantic models with revealed economic preference for real-time and explainable patent valuation
papers.authors: Yoo Y., Kim S., Liu J.
papers.abstract: This study proposes the Economic Reasoning Alignment via Instruction Tuning (ERA) framework, which aligns the semantic reasoning of Large Language Models (LLMs) with revealed economic preferences to establish a new paradigm for real-time and interpretable patent valuation. We theoretically conceptualize patent renewal history as a revealed economic preference and leverage it as an objective supervisory signal to align the generative reasoning of LLMs with market realities, a process we term Eco-Semantic Alignment. Our empirical analysis of 10,000 randomly sampled European Patent Office patents across diverse domains confirms the efficacy of this approach. The ERA framework achieves superior performance across all evaluated metrics compared to the baseline models. Specifically, it surpasses the traditional Random Forest model based on TF-IDF features by 36.3% in accuracy, 33.1% in Macro-F1, and 88.1% in the Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). Against the discriminative pre-trained language model Longformer, ERA exhibits gains of 11.5% in accuracy, 8.7% in Macro-F1, and 27.4% in MCC. It also exceeds the zero-shot performance of the generative LLM GPT-5-mini by 9.6% in accuracy, 8.3% in Macro-F1, and 21.5% in MCC. The ablation study confirms the criticality of the Rationale Generation module (Economic Chain-of-Thought), whose removal led to the largest performance decline, with a 6.4% relative drop in Macro-F1. Moreover, ERA demonstrates robust applicability across heterogeneous patent landscapes.

papers.title: A cooperative game-based compensation allocation mechanism for consensus in group decision-making
papers.authors: Shen Y., Han X., Zhan J., Bao Y.
papers.abstract: In group decision-making processes, achieving consensus often requires decision-makers to adjust their initial preferences, which incurs adjustment costs and may be constrained by individual budget limitations. Existing consensus models mainly focus on optimizing preference adjustments, while insufficient attention has been paid to budget feasibility and compensation allocation. To bridge this gap, this study proposes a consensus compensation analysis framework that explicitly incorporates individual budget constraints and external compensation. We first develop a budget feasibility diagnostic model to evaluate whether a target consensus level can be achieved under given budget conditions and to determine the minimum required compensation. Building on this, a minimum cost consensus model incorporating individual budgets and compensation is constructed, and its feasibility conditions are derived. To address situations of budget shortfalls, two compensation allocation mechanisms are designed based on Nash bargaining and the Shapley value, respectively. An illustrative example inspired by the Taihu Lake Basin, involving eight decision-makers and four governance alternatives, demonstrates the implementation process. Sensitivity analysis and comparative experiments demonstrate the feasibility, fairness, and robustness of the proposed framework under limited budgets.

papers.title: Focus on latent: Toward a meaningful and interpretable latent representation for diffusion models
papers.authors: Yu Z., Yang Z., Zhang W., Liu Z., Liu Y.
papers.abstract: Diffusion models achieve high-fidelity data generation but remain limited by poor interpretability, restricting their use in applications requiring semantically grounded representations. Existing methods to enhancing the interpretability either rely on post-hoc analysis that passively reveal latent semantics or extract unconstrained latent representations, often failing to produce latent representations with clear semantic meaning and discriminative capacity. To address this, we propose a diffusion model Focus on Latent, FcLDiff, which aims to explicitly learn semantically meaningful and interpretable latent representations without introducing post-hoc analysis components that require additional training. Our method employs a dual strategy: a constraint-driven optimization strategy compels the latent representation to capture the core semantics of the data by leveraging semantic encoders along with a mutual information constraint; simultaneously, a mechanism-guided modulation strategy further directs the model’s focus toward the latent representation through a feature weighting mechanism, which adaptively modulates the hierarchical importance of skip and backbone features within the UNet architecture. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of FcLDiff across classification, generation, and disentanglement tasks. On four benchmark datasets, FcLDiff achieves a maximum gain of 0.224 in classification accuracy and a 0.202 improvement in the TAD disentanglement metric. On a materials microstructure dataset, it achieves a classification accuracy of 0.983 and generates smooth, semantically coherent interpolations, highlighting its strong potential for interpretable generative modeling and scientific analysis.

papers.title: Multimodal large language model-driven entity alignment via hierarchical interaction
papers.authors: Peng J., Zha Y., Shan Y., Wang X.
papers.abstract: Multi-modal entity alignment aims to identify equivalent entities across different multi-modal knowledge graphs. However, existing methods represent a bottleneck due to two primary limitations: insufficient fine-grained cross-modal semantic associations caused by decoupled encoding, and incoherent semantic-structural interactions resulting from modality heterogeneity. To address these issues, we design a unified framework that integrates a multi-modal large language model-driven semantic perception module with a hierarchical semantic-structural interaction strategy. First, to resolve the insufficient associations, the framework builds a semantic perception module that jointly encodes textual and visual attributes through adaptive token fusion and contrastive learning, which not only enhances cross-modal modeling but also enables robust representation learning under limited labeled data. Second, to mitigate incoherent interactions, we propose a hierarchical interaction strategy that integrates feature-level alignment for structural-semantic consistency as the foundation, with semantic-level alignment for task-oriented output coherence as the refinement. Extensive experiments on five widely used benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms recent state-of-the-art baselines, achieving improvements such as an average increase of 2.4% in Hits@1 on FBDB15K and 3.5% on FBYG15K. Furthermore, our analyses under low-supervision settings reveal that the framework remains highly effective, highlighting its robustness and generalization capability.

papers.title: ALD2[jls-end-space/]: Adaptive layer-wise denoising decoding for hallucinations mitigation in large vision-language models
papers.authors: Zhou Y., Yang M., Zhang J., Li J., Feng S.
papers.abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have shown strong reasoning capabilities by leveraging Large language models (LLMs). However, hallucination remains a challenge for many LVLMs. Through our experiments, we identify that existing noise in shallow layers often leads to unstable token predictions during reasoning. We find that visual token pruning technologies along with multiplicative decoding effectively mitigate this interference. Building on this insight, we propose Adaptive Layer-wise Denoising Decoding (ALD2[jls-end-space/]), a novel framework that mitigates hallucinations within LVLMs by dynamically selecting an optimal shallow layer for visual-token pruning and multiplicatively fusing the denoised distributions with that of the final layer. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks (CHAIR with 500 images; POPE with 500 images; MME with 2374 cases) demonstrate that ALD2 consistently improves the accuracy across multiple LVLMs. For example, we achieve an average accuracy improvement of 5.61% on POPE metrics using the InstructBlip-Vicuna-7B model and an increase of 88.56 MME score points in the MME evaluation benchmark with the LLaVA-Next-8B model. papers.authors: Jung W., Kim A.H., Hung Y., Chear C., Shah V., Ammari T.
papers.abstract: We present a novel pipeline for poverty assessment using social media and apply it to a dataset of 1.2 million geotagged tweets from Zambia. Our findings show that the tweets from poorer villages emphasize local, concrete needs, whereas those from wealthier villages focus on abstract development concepts. We also compare imputation methods for data-sparse contexts and find that kriging improves predictive accuracy by 15 % over standard approaches, while providing uncertainty quantification for adaptive sampling. This work demonstrates the viability of social media discourse as a participatory, scalable poverty monitoring tool in regions with limited data.

papers.title: Multi-view learning with hierarchical cross-attention for next POI recommendation
papers.authors: Sang C.Y., Hu X.B., Liao S.G., Hu C.Q., Wen J.H.
papers.abstract: AbstractNext point-of-interest (POI) recommendation aims to predict a user’s next destination from historical check-in behavior. Many existing methods handle sequential, spatial, and semantic information in separate modules and combine them at later stages, making it challenging to capture how sequential patterns influence spatial choices, how geographic context shapes semantic preferences, and how category transitions guide temporal decisions. We propose MvHCA-POI, a multi-view framework with hierarchical cross-attention that enables cross-view feature integration during encoding. MvHCA-POI builds three graph-based views: a category sequence graph, a POI sequence graph, and a geographic graph that captures both local proximity and global structural relationships. Unlike traditional methods that integrate view embeddings at a late fusion stage, our hierarchical cross-attention operates in two stages. The category sequence first guides token-level enhancements within each view, emphasizing relevant recent check-ins and nearby POIs, and then serves as a semantic bridge to align view-level representations across different views. Experiments on four real-world LBSN datasets demonstrate that MvHCA-POI achieves 6.5% to 11.2% improvements over state-of-the-art baselines in standard ranking metrics. Ablation studies further confirm the contribution of each component in the hierarchical cross-attention framework.

papers.title: GLINT: Global–local fusion with attention intervention for MLLM hallucination mitigation caused by insufficient visual resolution
papers.authors: Zhao P., Xu J., Zhang S., Wang C., Han W.
papers.abstract: Existing hallucination mitigation methods for MLLMs, such as contrastive decoding and visual attention enhancement, often struggle with small objects. To address this issue, we propose GLINT, a training-free framework inspired by the global-to-local strategy of human vision to mitigate hallucinations. GLINT introduces a semantic-driven global–local encoding component to automatically crop informative regions, an attention-guided masking strategy, and an attention intervention mechanism to encourage balanced utilization of global image, local image, and language. Additionally, it integrates contrastive decoding with an auxiliary text-only model to suppress hallucinations induced by language priors. Extensive experiments on nine widely used datasets show that GLINT outperforms the SOTA method by an average of 1.1 F1-score points.

papers.title: Mining temporally aware patterns with fuzzy utility measures under dynamically moving window environments
papers.authors: Kim D., Park S., Park J., Kim H., Ryu T., Yun U.
papers.abstract: Mining high temporal fuzzy utility patterns from data streams is important for interpretable real-time information processing. However, prior incremental methods that handle the entire data suffer from inefficiency with the continuous stream arrival, which is problematic in real-time information processing environments. Moreover, handling concept drift is critical, as the data distribution changes over time and information from older data becomes less representative in current conditions. To handle the limitation, a novel approach is introduced for extracting high temporal fuzzy utility patterns from data streams, adopting dynamically moving windows via a sliding window strategy to handle concept drift. Rather than processing the entire accumulated streams, the proposed approach efficiently manages the most recent fixed-size batches. Furthermore, pruning strategies optimized for the moving window are adopted to minimize the search space. Comprehensive evaluations on six real-world datasets with four membership functions indicate that the proposed approach demonstrates enhanced runtime performance with competitive memory usage, achieving up to 40% improvement in runtime. Scalability evaluation demonstrates its scalability across five increasing transaction sizes, showing at least 1.34 times smaller runtime growth than comparison methods under on-par memory usage. Statistical performance on 30 sampled thresholds and sensitivity analyses show its stable efficiency to parameter variations, while accuracy analysis on a total of 240 samples indicates that it obtains results without any pattern loss. Moreover, the analysis of result pattern characteristics reveals that the proposed approach effectively captures recent data trends, and the case study under the concept drift shows its applicability in various stream environments.

papers.title: Deciphering oracle bone characters: Pictographic captioning and reasoning for morphological recognition
papers.authors: Wang Y., Li Z., Liang D., Zhang Y., Pan S., Fang Y.
papers.abstract: Oracle Bone Characters (OBCs) represent the earliest mature writing system in China, yet their intricate structures and diverse variants pose significant challenges for automated decipherment. This paper proposes the Pictographic Captioning and Reasoning (PCR) framework, reformulating OBC decipherment from a traditional image recognition problem into a visual-language semantic reasoning task. Emulating the logic of human paleographers, PCR adopts a two-stage pipeline. First, a Large Multimodal Model (LMM), fine-tuned with domain knowledge, generates fine-grained pictographic descriptions to explicitly characterize structural compositions and visual attributes. Subsequently, by integrating these captions with the Oracle Bone Studies Knowledge Base (OBS-KB), a Large Language Model (LLM) performs semantic inference to determine glyph categories. We evaluate the framework on a dataset of 600 OBC categories, each associated with an Ideographic Description Sequence (IDS) and 30 generated captions. Results demonstrate that PCR significantly outperforms existing character-level and radical-level methods. Notably, in open-set scenarios for unseen glyphs, PCR achieves a flexible accuracy exceeding 49%. This research demonstrates the efficacy of coupling visual perception with linguistic reasoning and provides a novel modeling perspective for OBC decipherment.

papers.title: Unveiling heterogeneity in tourist-generated content quality: A large language model approach with multi-dimensional analysis
papers.authors: Gao J., Chen L., Lin W., Peng P., Xu Y., Lan T., Lu F., Claramunt C.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of tourist-generated content demands scalable and reliable quality assessment methods. This study introduces an LLM-driven framework that combines parameter-efficient fine-tuning and prompt engineering to evaluate content quality accurately and interpretably. Applied to 484,930 reviews from MaFengWo, TripAdvisor, and Ctrip, the approach achieves superior performance (RMSE=0.3040, NDCG@100=0.500, BERTScore=77.95%) with 9 × higher efficiency. Spatial-temporal-semantic analyses reveal platform-specific quality patterns: MaFengWo exhibits prominent spatial centrality and stable temporal cointegration; TripAdvisor demonstrates simplified core-periphery structures with high volatility; Ctrip presents dynamic multicentricity particularly in Shanghai. Two domestic platforms, MaFengWo and Ctrip, expose systematic deficiency on the theme ‘Decision-making Plan’ (92.9∼96.4% lacking operational suggestions), while international TripAdvisor emphasizes ‘Practical Information’ and ‘Consumption Activity’ but 40.76% neglects original viewpoints. Heterogeneous network analysis identifies the behavioral signatures of high-reliability user—preference attachment, quality stability, and profile homogeneity. This work bridges theoretical rigor with operational scalability, demonstrating the potential of LLMs in content governance for digital tourism.

papers.title: How does digital hoarding affect user resistance to social media switching behavior: The role of nostalgia, inertia and mindfulness
papers.authors: Jia M., Zhao Y., Zhang X., Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Social media has afforded users unprecedented affordances for accumulating digital content and fragments and emerged as a fundamental space for digital hoarding and emotional connection, increasing the likelihood that consumers will remain on existing platforms due to resource lock-in, path dependency, or social connections. This study identifies a mechanism linking digital hoarding on social media to user switching resistance, grounded in conservation of resources theory. We conducted an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, involving quantitative analysis of a three-wave time-lagged survey of 316 social media users from an initial pool of 725 using SmartPLS 4.0 and 20 follow-up interviews for qualitative interpretation. Findings reveal that digital hoarding on social media directly predicts user resistance to switching, while also driving nostalgia and inertia, which subsequently influence user resistance to switching. Mindfulness moderates the effect of inertia and digital hoarding on user resistance to switching. Further multigroup analysis demonstrates that there are generational differences in the pathways of our model. Augmenting these findings, the interview data offer a more nuanced explanation regarding how the above five constructs materialize and how digital hoarding contexts function and interact with nostalgia and inertia as users engage in resistance to switching. Importantly, the qualitative evidence also captures several novel insights that extend beyond the scope of the quantitative results. Our research brings valuable insights into the dynamic processes underlying user resistance to switching in the social media context from a novel perspective and challenges mainstream calls to eliminate digital hoarding by highlighting its role in fostering user stickiness and informing platform design strategies for digital consumption experiences.

papers.title: Stochastic dynamics of competitive information dissemination in cyber–physical integrated networks
papers.authors: Chen J., Lu D., Han R., Shu J., Zhang G.
papers.abstract: The integration of physical and cyber networks can be a double-edged dynamic. While it accelerates the dissemination of positive information, it also intensifies the diffusion of negative information. A clear understanding of the stochastic dynamics of competitive information dissemination is essential. It enables effective control strategies to curb the spread of negative information and maintain social stability. However, designing and controlling the dissemination of competitive information in cyber–physical integrated networks (CPINs) is challenging due to competition and stochasticity. Moreover, the heterogeneity of CPINs further aggravates this problem. To address this, we propose a competitive information dissemination method to capture and control the stochastic dynamics in CPINs. Specifically, we build a CPIN model to characterize the heterogeneity between physical and cyber networks. Furthermore, we develop a temporal point process-based competitive information dissemination model (TPP-CIDM) that captures the stochastic evolution of both positive and negative information. This dissemination model quantifies the stochastic dynamics by computing the probability distribution of the sizes of competitive information, reducing biases inherent in deterministic solutions. Finally, we design an event-driven optimal control (EOC) strategy to dynamically modulate the intervention intensity. The intervention optimization problem is formulated to maximize utility under cost constraints, and a heuristic solution is provided. Numerical simulations on both synthetic and real-world networks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: NMFL: Coupling probabilistic diffusion dynamics with fitness landscape analysis for influence maximization problem in social networks
papers.authors: Geng L., Tang J., Zhao F., Pang J., Zhang S.
papers.abstract: Existing meta-heuristics for the NP-hard Influence Maximization (IM) problem are often constrained by inefficient fitness evaluation and a lack of structural awareness. To address these challenges, this study proposes NMFL, a fitness landscape-aware discrete Nelder–Mead algorithm. Specifically, a Probabilistic Recursion Estimation (PRE) fitness function, modeled on the Bernoulli distribution, which utilizes engineering linearization and Taylor series approximations, is developed to balance evaluation accuracy with computational efficiency. Furthermore, the discrete solution space is mapped onto a fitness landscape, where a novel discrete centroid indicator is introduced to guide evolutionary trajectories and rectify search deviations. Experimental results on six real-world networks, ranging from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of nodes, demonstrate that NMFL outperforms mainstream meta-heuristics by an average of 8.1% in influence spread. Crucially, it achieves solution quality comparable to greedy benchmarks while reducing computational time by several orders of magnitude, offering a scalable blueprint for decoding IM dynamics.

papers.title: Latent diffusion-augmented cross-modal representation learning for radiology report generation
papers.authors: Hou X., Li X., Wang S., Lu M., Lin H., Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Radiology report generation aims to produce comprehensive textual descriptions from medical images, enhancing diagnostic efficiency and alleviating the workload of radiologists. However, it often suffers from weak semantic expression of subtle lesions and inherent heterogeneity between visual and textual modalities. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework, Latent Diffusion-augmented Cross-modal Representation learning (LDCR), which enhances pathological representations and promotes deep cross-modal alignment. Specifically, LDCR introduces a Latent Diffusion Enhancement Module (LDEM) that simulates progressive degradation and semantic reconstruction in latent space through a diffusion mechanism, improving sensitivity to subtle pathological lesions. Building on latent diffusion-enhanced visual representation, a Heterogeneous Information Fusion Module (HIFM) is devised to bridge the modality gap by aligning visual and textual features in a shared semantic space Extensive experiments on two public benchmarks, IU X-ray and MIMIC-CXR, demonstrate that LDCR outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods across multiple evaluation metrics, achieving improvements of up to 1.5%, 0.8% and 3.5% in BLEU-4, METEOR and ROUGE-L on IU X-ray, and 3.7%, 1.9% and 1.7% on MIMIC-CXR, respectively. papers.title: Linguistic preference relations with weakened hedges embedded graph model for water resource conflict resolution
papers.authors: Yao X., Ren T., Zeng X.J., Xu Z.
papers.abstract: The graph model for conflict resolution (GMCR) has emerged as an effective approach for addressing strategy conflicts. Within this framework, decision-makers (DMs) are required to furnish their preference information for every conceivable scenario. While existing research commonly assumes that DMs utilize quantitative representation formats, in certain real-life contexts, they may rely on qualitative assessments based on their cognitive expression habits. The linguistic terms with weakened hedges (LTWHs), designed to address the uncertainty inherent in single terms, serve as an effective tool for modelling linguistic expressions in natural languages. This paper presents a novel GMCR framework incorporating LTWHs to capture qualitative and uncertain preferences. Furthermore, this study presents develop four new stability definitions tailored for both two-DM and n-DM scenarios under linguistic contexts. Our method also addresses preference inconsistencies among composite stakeholders. Finally, to prove the practicality and utility of our proposed model, an illustrative example centred around a conflict of the Yellow River Basin in China is provided. The results reveal that incorporating LTWHs leads to more nuanced and realistic equilibrium outcomes, highlighting the influence of DMs’ linguistic characteristics on conflict resolution.

papers.title: BFDM: Continual relation extraction via bidirectional feedback and dynamic multi-teacher knowledge distillation
papers.authors: Hang T., Li D., Xu Z., Feng J.
papers.abstract: Continual Relation Extraction (CRE) aims to continuously learn new relations while preventing the forgetting of previously learned relations. However, existing methods still face significant challenges in effectively retaining and utilizing prior knowledge, and their performance is strongly influenced by the degree of task fusion. To address these challenges, we propose a CRE model based on Bidirectional Feedback and Dynamic Multi-teacher knowledge distillation (BFDM). The model significantly enhances the fusion of current and historical tasks through the bidirectional feedback module, enabling new-task learning and memory-replay learning to relearn from each other via feedback. Additionally, the dynamic multi-teacher knowledge distillation module saves the optimal parameters for each new task into separate teacher models, which are then sequentially distilled into the student model during the memory replay learning phase. This ensures accurate and consistent retention of prior knowledge. With an average accuracy of 92.45% and 88.61% on the two benchmark datasets, BFDM demonstrates promising performance, highlighting its potential as a competitive state-of-the-art model. Ablation studies further validated the effectiveness of the BFDM model. Removing any module resulted in varying degrees of decline in average accuracy across both datasets. The maximum drop when removing a single module reached 1.18% and 1.37%, respectively. Our source code is available at https://github.com/lids316/BFDM.

papers.title: Information-aware valuation and dynamic pricing for textual data in mobile environments
papers.authors: Xiong W., Wang Y., Li W., Guo H., Zhang J., Wang H.
papers.abstract: Data has become a fundamental asset in the information age. However, the absence of generalizable valuation and pricing frameworks poses significant challenges for data trading. This study proposes an information-aware valuation method for textual data based on weighted perplexity entropy (WPE), along with a dynamic pricing mechanism grounded in reinforcement learning (RL). For data valuation, we first evaluate the proposed WPE method across three heterogeneous textual datasets, followed by robustness assessments under noise injection scenarios. For data pricing, we formulate it as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with the objective of profit maximization, incorporating an early submission incentive to encourage timely data contributions. Two different pricing strategies are developed, considering both immediate and long-term profits. Experimental results demonstrate that our WPE valuation method and RL-based pricing strategies consistently outperform existing valuation and pricing baselines. Specifically, our pricing strategies can increase an additional 16%, 80%, and 230% profit compared to three selected baselines. These findings further underscore the theoretical relevance of linking information theory with data economics, and the practical value of enabling more efficient and informed data acquisition.

papers.title: MFND-DCL: Multimodal fake news detection based on dual contrastive learning
papers.authors: Qian M., Guo S., Chen Y., Wang C., Ye Z.

To address these issues, this study proposes MFND-DCL, a Multimodal Fake News Detection framework based on Dual Contrastive Learning. At the cross-modal level, we align text and image features in a shared semantic space via contrastive loss, thereby capturing cross-modal consistency. At the inter-sample level, supervised contrastive learning is employed to optimize the feature space layout, enhancing the distinction between samples that are semantically similar but differ in veracity. Experiments conducted on the Weibo (N = 9,527 posts) and PHEME (N = 5,802 tweets) datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing baseline models in both accuracy and F1 score, achieving accuracies of 95.5% and 90.1%, respectively. Moreover, the method maintains stable performance across different language scenarios, validating the effectiveness and robustness of dual contrastive learning. This study offers new perspectives for the early identification of fake news. We release the code and data at https://github.com/chenyujia-max/MFND-DCL.

papers.title: Benchmarking and enhancing the ability of large language models on event generalization
papers.authors: Shao S., Wen T., Dong Y., Ke P., Qin K.
papers.abstract: Event generalization represents the mapping from specific events to abstract events, which is vital for information extraction tasks. Despite the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) on various information extraction tasks, their capability in event generalization is still under-explored due to the lack of open-source benchmark datasets. In this work, we construct the first open-source dataset ElizBench for event generalization, with 5757 data samples and 85 abstract event classes. We not only systematically benchmark mainstream LLMs on ElizBench, but also propose the Stepwise Self-Rethinking Event Generalization (SSR-EG) framework to further enhance LLMs’ performance. This framework stimulates LLMs to leverage their internal knowledge to rethink their responses step-by-step without introducing any external information. Experimental results show that ElizBench identifies deficiencies in existing LLMs when dealing with event generalization. Meanwhile, our proposed SSR-EG framework consistently enhances the performance of LLMs with various scales, improving their weighted F1 scores by 2.03% on average over direct prompting.

papers.title: VTFAformer: A visual–tactile fusion network for object attribute recognition
papers.authors: Yi Z., Chen G., Wang H., Li L., Li B., Qi F.

To effectively integrate visual and tactile data, we propose VTFAformer, a novel framework that introduces a task-oriented, pre-fusion alignment stage. This stage compels the model to disentangle and extract modality-invariant core concepts (i.e., attributes), which significantly enhances synergistic reasoning between the visual and tactile modalities. Extensive experiments were conducted on five public datasets (encompassing a total of 275K samples): TacQuad, ObjectFolder Real, ObjectFolder 2.0, ObjectFolder 1.0, and Touch and Go. Compared to existing state-of-the-art visual–tactile fusion algorithms, our method achieves an average improvement of 1.78% in mA and 2.41% in Acc. These findings demonstrate VTFAformer’s multimodal advantage in environmental perception, highlighting its potential in processing heterogeneous sensor data.

papers.title: AMART: A multi-agent reflective framework for detecting and correcting faithfulness errors in translation
papers.authors: Li J., Zhu S., Xiong D.
papers.abstract: Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated unprecedented capabilities in machine translation. However, their practical deployment in high-stakes applications is critically hindered by the generation of “hallucinations”—content detached from the source text, which severely compromises translational faithfulness. Furthermore, relying on unconditional self-correction often proves counterproductive, as models may blindly alter originally faithful translations or overlook subtle errors without explicit multi-dimensional guidance. To address this fundamental limitation, we propose AMART, a Multi-Agent Reflective framework designed to instill a structured, two-stage deliberative process into the translation workflow of LLMs. In AMART, we first employ a multi-agent detection system where specialized agents, operating at complementary granularities (sentence, chunk, and word), collaboratively scrutinize an initial translation for potential faithfulness deviations. If an error is flagged, AMART initiates a conditional reflective process, which first prompts the LLM to analyze and articulate the nature of the identified error, and only then guides it to regenerate a corrected translation based on its own reflection. This mechanism compels the model to form a metacognitive understanding of its failure modes, moving beyond simple error correction. Extensive experiments on challenging hallucination benchmarks show that AMART improves hallucination detection accuracy by up to 1.3-fold and substantially reduces faithfulness errors. On the WMT24++ and FLORES-200 test sets, the framework consistently improves overall translation quality and achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming strong baselines by up to 2.2 BLEU and 2.4 COMET points. Ablation and efficiency analyses further indicate that the conditionally triggered architecture allows diagnostic signals to guide targeted corrections, improving semantic faithfulness while keeping inference cost manageable.

papers.title: Label distribution-driven semantic discrimination enhanced hashing for cross-modal retrieval
papers.authors: Qi G., Zhou X., Huang C.
papers.abstract: Supervised hashing leverages labels as semantic supervision to mitigate cross-modal heterogeneity, however, traditional methods that rely solely on logical labels capture only binary relationships, failing to explore deeper sample-label correlations Moreover, a major challenge in cross-modal retrieval is how to embed semantic supervision to eliminate inter-modal heterogeneity while preserving sufficient multi-modal features. To tackle the above issues, this paper introduces a two-stage cross-modal hashing (CMH) method, dubbed Label Distribution-Driven Semantic Discrimination Enhanced Hashing (L3DEH) for cross-modal retrieval. In the label reconstruction stage, semantic classification centers and the nuclear norm are incorporated to integrate modal structural information into the reconstructed labels. Constraints are also introduced to ensure the labels reflect classification importance while preserving the original classification information. Secondly, to account for the characteristics of real-value labels, a novel label semantic similarity metric is designed to hierarchically process relationships among samples. Additionally, an asymmetric optimization strategy is adopted to eliminate heterogeneity across modalities. These approaches effectively embed semantic features into hash codes, enhancing discriminative power. Comprehensive experiments on MIRFlickr-25K, IAPR-TC12, and NUS-WIDE datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, with L3DEH achieving average mAP improvements of 0.8%, 0.2%, and 1.1%, respectively. Furthermore, despite its more complex two-stage design, L3DEH incurs no significant increase in training time, as verified by both complexity analysis and empirical runtime comparisons.

papers.title: Generative AI and cloud deployment for intelligent systems: a retrieval-augmented generation framework using amazon bedrock
papers.authors: Guettala M., Bourekkache S., Kazar O., Harous S.
papers.abstract: The growing demand for scalable, semantically grounded intelligent systems has revealed limitations in many current generative AI deployments, including weak contextual grounding, static rule-based adaptation, and inconsistent latency under cloud-based orchestration. This study presents UL-RagCloud, a cloud-native Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed to operationalize the infrastructural and semantic foundations of ubiquitous learning environments. Ubiquitous learning (UL) systems can be conceptualized as comprising multiple interdependent layers, including infrastructural scalability, adaptive interaction mechanisms, and learner-level outcome evaluation. The present study focuses on the infrastructural and adaptive layers required to ensure reliable and safe integration of generative AI within UL environments. The architecture integrates Amazon Titan Text Embeddings, OpenSearch Serverless, and Claude v3 Sonnet via Amazon Bedrock within a stateless, serverless pipeline that supports domain-sensitive semantic context-awareness at the query level and evidence-grounded response generation. UL-RagCloud enables real-time question answering by dynamically retrieving semantically indexed content and generating contextually grounded responses through a stateless, serverless pipeline. The framework is empirically evaluated using the SQuAD v2.0 dataset, comprising 10,570 question–answer pairs across 1,204 documents. Retrieval performance is assessed using Grounded Contextual Retrieval Evaluation (GCRE), achieving high Context Precision (87.75%), Recall (90.12%), and F1 Score (88.92%). Semantic answer quality is evaluated via RAGAS metrics, demonstrating strong Faithfulness (86.9%), low Hallucination (13.1%), and high Answer Relevancy (79.9%). These results demonstrate UL-RagCloud’s robustness and efficiency as a cloud-native, query-level semantic adaptation framework supporting evidence-grounded interaction in ubiquitous learning infrastructures. papers.title: Mapping scholarly knowledge: A systematic review of Knowledge Graphs for academic papers
papers.authors: Ramírez Molina A.A., Li S., Gong J.
papers.abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are vital for organizing the vast scholarly literature. However, existing research has predominantly focused on KGs that model relationships across documents, a paradigm we refer to as “inter-paper” KGs, often overlooking the rich internal semantic structure of individual papers. This gap limits the ability of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems to reason across different levels of abstraction, a capability that is essential for deep knowledge comprehension. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, this paper provides a systematic review and comparative analysis of KG approaches derived from academic literature, introducing a conceptual distinction between inter-paper (breadth-oriented) and the less-explored intra-paper (depth-oriented) KGs. We analyze 102 studies to map their methodologies, tools, datasets, applications, challenges, and future directions, and we incorporate a structured appraisal of methodological rigor and reproducibility. Our findings show that inter-paper approaches (81.4%) leverage scalable Natural Language Processing (NLP) and network analysis on large bibliographic databases for tasks such as recommendation and trend analysis. Conversely, intra-paper approaches (12.7%) prioritize precise extraction and detailed semantic modeling to support fine-grained reasoning within single documents. Large Language Models (LLMs) are an emerging trend for both categories. The study concludes that the key distinction lies in this breadth-versus-depth trade-off. Recognizing their complementary strengths, we argue that integrated, multi-granular KG systems are pivotal for advancing scholarly communication. Such systems can enhance the explainability of AI-driven insights by tracing findings to their evidential roots, provide robust grounding for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and facilitate machine-assisted scientific discovery, ultimately contributing to more interpretable, trustworthy, and intelligent systems for synthesizing scientific knowledge.

papers.title: When input perturbation outperforms gradient perturbation: Achieving high-accuracy deep learning under local differential privacy
papers.authors: Peng S., Zhang J., Hu C., Wu Q., Wang H., Yang M., Guo T.
papers.abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable success but remains vulnerable to privacy threats such as membership inference attacks (MIA), where adversaries infer the presence of specific user data in the training set. While differential privacy offers a theoretical framework naturally suited to defend against MIAs, existing implementations face significant challenges. Gradient perturbation methods typically rely on a trusted central server, posing risks of privacy leakage; conversely, input perturbation eliminates this trust assumption but often suffers from severe utility degradation due to excessive noise. To address these problems, we propose DL-LDP, a novel framework that alleviates the utility loss inherent in input perturbation through two key strategies. First, we employ a piecewise mechanism that applies bounded perturbation to normalized data, thereby maximizing the probability that perturbed values fall within high-utility intervals. Second, we integrate a strategic dropout mechanism during training to counteract model bias induced by the added noise. Theoretically, we show that DL-LDP generates perturbed data that maintains a linear correlation with original features, enabling the model to effectively learn latent representations, while the dropout technique reduces the misclassification of non-feature regions. Extensive experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that DL-LDP not only significantly outperforms traditional input perturbation methods but also surpasses state-of-the-art (SOTA) gradient perturbation techniques. Notably, on the CIFAR-10 dataset with a privacy budget of (Formula presented), DL-LDP achieves an accuracy increase of approximately 13% compared to SOTA gradient methods, while reducing the model loss from 1.397 to 0.520. DL-LDP enables individuals to contribute data for improving intelligent services without compromising their personal privacy to service providers.

papers.title: Towards distribution-aware active learning for data-efficient neural architecture predictor
papers.authors: Yu C., Wang Y., Tang C., Ju W., Liu X., Lv J.
papers.abstract: Neural Predictors (NPs) are pivotal for efficient Neural Architecture Search (NAS) but suffer from limited accuracy due to the high cost of acquiring labeled training data. While active learning (AL) can mitigate this by prioritizing informative samples, existing methods suffer from selection bias under imbalanced data distributions, often sacrificing representativeness for diversity. To address this, we redefine the sample selection mechanism in AL and propose a Distribution-aware Active Learning framework for Neural Predictor (called DARE). The goal is to select samples that not only ensure diversity but also exhibit a high degree of generalizability, making them more representative of the underlying data distribution. Our approach first extracts architecture representations via a graph-based encoder enhanced with a consistency-driven objective. Then, a two-stage selection strategy identifies both globally diverse and locally reliable samples through progressive representation learning and refinement. For non-uniform data distributions, we further introduce an adaptive mechanism that anchors sampling to key regions with high similarity density, avoiding performance degradation caused by outliers. Extensive experiments on NAS-Bench-101, NAS-Bench-201, NAS-Bench-301, and DARTS demonstrate that DARE achieves state-of-the-art prediction performance with extremely scarce labeled data. For instance, on NAS-Bench-101, it outperforms the second-best baseline by 4.29% in Kendall’s Tau with only 424 samples. Furthermore, DARE efficiently identifies optimal architectures using as few as 100 queries on DARTS.

papers.title: CIM: Interpretable model with consistency representation and prompt learning
papers.authors: Dong L., Li Z., Chen L., Zheng C., Peng X., Li Y., Cui X.
papers.abstract: Supervised learning that rely exclusively on class labels often suffer from insufficient guidance for training deep neural networks (DNNs), resulting in inherent model biases and limited interpretability. To address these challenges, this study introduces the Consistent Interpretable Model (CIM) for interpretable image classification. The proposed CIM is constructed based on three core components. First, causal inference analysis is employed to model the learning process of DNNs, establishing a theoretical foundation for identifying spurious feature-task correlations. Second, the unbiasedness of task features is ensured by aligning original image embeddings with task-relevant prior knowledge. Finally, rich semantic knowledge from contrastively pre-trained text encoders is exploited to strengthen the alignment between the model’s task feature distribution and real-world scenarios. Extensive experiments show that CIM substantially improves DNN performance, particularly in fine-grained and out-of-distribution classification (achieving over 8% improvement in Top-1 accuracy) tasks. Moreover, CIM outperforms existing methods in terms of causality (with over a 10% gain in Grad-CAM’s Overall metric) and consistency (with over a 4% gain in Grad-CAM’s CH metric) of model explanations. Additionally, the alignment of prompt text representations with task object representations in CIM enables textual explanations for DNN decisions.
