papers.title: Who am I? And who should I be? The use and trust effects of identity strategies in AI-generated science communication
papers.authors: Yang Z., Jiang Y., Tao R., Wu F.
papers.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen-AI) is now integral to science communication, but its identity strategies and their impact on audience trust are not well understood. To address these issues, this paper conducts two studies. Study 1 employs an algorithmic auditing method to analyse the identity strategies frequently used by Gen-AI in producing science communication content, revealing that Gen-AI more frequently adopts an expert identity rather than a layperson identity when generating science communication content. Different large models use these strategies differently, indicating that identities used by Gen-AI in science communication may be culturally informed. To further explore the trust effects of these identity strategies, the results of Study 2, an experimental study (n = 1304), indicate that audiences trust AI-generated science communication content more when it is framed using expert rather than layperson strategies. This effect is positively mediated by perceived process-based and institution-based trust but negatively mediated by characteristics-based trust. This mechanism shares some similarities with the human science communication scenario. Communicative context (Gen-AI vs. human) only negatively moderates the effect of identity strategies on perceived institution-based trust, indicating that expert strategies enhance institutional trust to a lesser extent in Gen-AI contexts than in human contexts. These results clarify the ‘anthropomorphic characteristics’ of Gen-AI in science communication and further suggest that using expert identity strategies in Gen-AI may be the better way to earn audience trust.

papers.title: LoTTA: Low-rank test-time adaptation for unsupervised tabular anomaly detection
papers.authors: Shang Y.M., Peng W., Huang W., Gu N., Zhang K.
papers.abstract: Unsupervised tabular anomaly detection aims to identify anomalous samples in tabular data without labeled examples, relying on the core assumption that the training set contains only normal samples. Consequently, existing methods typically force the model to overfit the training data, leveraging metrics such as the reconstruction error to separate anomalies during inference. However, due to the inherent limitation of the training data, it cannot encompass all possible normal patterns, which often causes existing methods to misclassify unseen normal samples as anomalies and lead to a high false positive rate. To address this issue, we propose LoTTA, a novel method that enhances the robustness of unsupervised tabular anomaly detection through Low-rank Test-Time Adaptation. Specifically, LoTTA operates in two stages. First, a pseudo-label generator is constructed by jointly training two self-supervised tasks with a shared encoder. Second, the low-rank test-time adaptation is performed, leveraging pseudo-labels to dynamically adjust the model to the normal distribution of test data while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Anomalies are finally identified based on the reconstruction error from the fine-tuned encoder–decoder model. Extensive experiments on 20 widely used benchmarks demonstrate that LoTTA achieves state-of-the-art performance, with an average AUC-PR across all datasets approximately 9.98% higher than that of previous leading models.

papers.title: Discriminative approximate low-rank projection with adaptive distance penalty for feature extraction
papers.authors: Liu Z., Liu S., Xiong H., Wu D., Ou W., Zhang K.
papers.abstract: With the increasing prevalence of high-dimensional images, it has become a popular research topic to find effective ways to extract their essential features. Latent low-rank representation (LatLRR) has emerged as a powerful unsupervised method for extracting salient features. However, LatLRR suffers from several limitations, including its unsupervised nature, inability to reduce feature dimensionality, and disregard for local manifold structures. To address these challenges, we propose a discriminative approximate low-rank projection with adaptive distance penalty (DALP-ADP), in which LatLRR is extended to the supervised scenarios by combining feature extraction with linear discriminant regression and a label relaxation matrix is introduced to enhance inter-class separability. Additionally, the low-rank projection is approximated by two different matrices to learn the features of any dimension. Furthermore, an adaptive distance penalty is incorporated to construct a weighted affinity graph, preserving both global and local structural relationships among samples. Extensive experiments on diverse image datasets demonstrate that DALP-ADP outperforms ten state-of-the-art methods, achieving good classification accuracy and robustness.

papers.title: Synergistic denoising: Dual-correction of semantic control and distribution optimization for sequential recommendation
papers.authors: Zhu Y., Wang G., Duan H., Wang Y., Liu P., Guo L., Lu R.
papers.abstract: Sequential recommendation aims to predict a user’s next interaction based on their historical behavior. While diffusion models have advanced sequential recommendation by capturing user uncertainty, they suffer from a fundamental challenge: distribution misalignment. This issue arises when models compress a user’s multi-dimensional interests into a single representation for conditional guidance, causing the generated distribution to deviate from true user preferences. We propose DSCDO, a framework that resolves this challenge through a Dual-correction of Semantic Control and Distribution Optimization. It synergistically integrates two components: (1) an orthogonal semantic decomposition module that projects the user’s interaction history into non-interfering semantic subspaces, thereby preventing the collapse of multifaceted user preferences into a single, over-generalized representation, and (2) an gradient enhance denoising network that employs a score-matching objective to explicitly model the gradient of the true preference distribution, thereby applying a precise, single-step adjustment to the initial prediction to directly fix the distribution misalignment. Experiments on four real-world datasets show DSCDO achieves 2.3%–16.75% improvements in HR@20 and 1.9%–9.14% gains in NDCG@20 over state-of-the-art baselines.11https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DSCDO.

papers.title: Domain-spanning migration dilemma of serial entrepreneurs in reward-based crowdfunding: Information-based breakthrough strategies
papers.authors: Liu H., Wang W., Han X., Xiao L.
papers.abstract: Knowledge about whether serial entrepreneurs in reward-based crowdfunding face the domain-spanning migration dilemma and corresponding information-based breakthrough strategies is still limited. Based on signaling theory, this study aims to mitigate this gap by using 28,438 serial entrepreneurs and their 74,978 projects on Kickstarter. We employ text mining methods to identify domain-spanning migration and classify information-based breakthrough strategies into two types: reward value and risk prospect (risk disclosure and prospect hint). The findings indicate that domain-spanning migration reduces the success odds of serial entrepreneurs by 57.5%. Compared with cognitive value-based rewards, functional value-based rewards and symbolic value-based rewards can weaken the migration penalty by 28.7% and 24%, respectively. Risk disclosure and prospect hint can enhance the migration penalty by 11.8% and 22.6%, respectively. This highlights that serial entrepreneurs who engage in domain-spanning migration should rationally design their information disclosure strategies, seeking a balance in information to maintain crowdfunding transparency while effectively mitigating the migration penalty. The post-hoc analysis indicates that the propensity of serial entrepreneurs to migrate is affected by the first-time entrepreneurial results. This study provides both theoretical basis and practical insights for serial entrepreneurs and platform managers to break the migration dilemma through information strategies.

papers.authors: Yang C., Gao W., Yu S., Chen Y., Qin Y., Huang R., Lin C.
papers.abstract: Legal case retrieval (LCR) requires ranking precedents according to their legal relevance, which is often poorly captured by surface-level semantic similarities alone. We propose a multiview retrieval framework that augments strong text encoders with structured factual representations extracted from case descriptions. Specifically, an instruction-tuned Llama3-8B model is prompted to produce an ordered event chain and participant roles under a constrained schema. We encode both the raw text and extracted structure and combine four complementary similarity signals—text similarity, event-chain similarity, event-type overlap, and role-aware alignment—via a learnable non-negative score aggregator. To support deployment at the corpus scale, candidate-side extraction and embeddings are computed offline and cached, and online inference is used to perform a single query-side extraction followed by artificial-neural-network retrieval and re-ranking over a small top-K shortlist. Experiments on two Chinese LCR benchmarks (LeCaRD and CAIL2022-LCR) demonstrate consistent gains over strong baselines, yielding a 3%-5% improvement in NDCG@K and better top-K retrieval quality. Qualitative analyses demonstrate that aligning matched events and participant roles provides interpretable evidence for retrieved results, which is valuable in legal applications.

papers.title: LiteKV: A KV cache compression method for efficient inference on resource-constrained devices
papers.authors: Zhang Z., Ilvovsky D.
papers.abstract: Transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) rely on Key-Value (KV) cache to accelerate autoregressive decoding, but memory and compute requirements still grow with context length, limiting deployment on resource-constrained devices. Existing training-free KV cache compression methods mainly rely on attention-driven retention heuristics, which may under preserve structurally informative tokens under tight cache budgets, especially when such tokens are not strongly highlighted by local or cumulative attention signals. As a result, long-range evidence and semantic continuity can be weakened in long-context inference. We propose LiteKV, a training-free KV cache management strategy that addresses this limitation with a three-ring cache structure and a Semantic Shift Awareness (SSA) mechanism. LiteKV maintains a recent window, a heavy-hitter region, and an overview zone, while SSA introduces a semantic-momentum signal to complement attention-based retention and improve the preservation of transition-relevant tokens. We evaluate LiteKV on Qwen 3, Llama 3.1, and Mistral 7B models against Full KV, StreamingLLM, H2[jls-end-space/]O, and SnapKV on several tasks. On LongPPL over 20k tokens from WikiText-103, LiteKV reduces perplexity from 12.74 for H2[jls-end-space/]O to 10.68, corresponding to a 16.2% reduction. In the Needle-in-a-Haystack task, LiteKV’s retrieval accuracy matches the Full KV baseline in several segments and remains substantially stronger than H2[jls-end-space/]O and StreamingLLM in entity-specific retrieval. LiteKV also remains robust on L-Eval benchmark under aggressive compression. For example, on Qwen3-30B with a 3.125% cache budget, LiteKV retains 83.5% of the Full KV score on meeting summarization task and 99.1% on review summarization task. These results suggest a favorable memory–quality trade-off for long-context inference across multiple model families.

papers.title: Multiple minds are better than one: Enhancing temporal knowledge graph forecasting with mixture of diverse graph experts
papers.authors: Xin Y., Shen H., Li S., Cheng Z., Liu X., Wu J., Zhou F.
papers.abstract: Temporal knowledge graph forecasting (TKGF) focuses on inferring future events by effectively modeling and utilizing past factual information. Although recent structure-aware methods excel at modeling dynamic event correlations, they often lack semantic-aware capabilities. Meanwhile, semantic-aware methods suffer from two main limitations: (1) insufficient modeling of evolving properties, and (2) gap between graph and LLMs. To tackle these challenges, we propose FMOGE, a novel Flexible Mixture Of diverse Graph Experts framework that performs fast thinking for global contextual facts and slow thinking for local logic rules, thereby enabling structural-semantic joint learning. Specifically, FMOGE consists of three complementary components: (1) The evolution-aware expert models the dynamic structural evolution of entities and relations across different facts. (2) The context-aware expert captures global contextual semantic knowledge from query-dependent contextual graphs via context-aware graph encoders, serving as a global shallow reasoner. (3) The logic-aware expert iteratively mines temporal logic rules through a rule-induced graph attention mechanism, enabling deep local reasoning. Furthermore, we design a hierarchical dynamic merging strategy that enhances each expert’s representation with relation-guided signals and adaptively integrates their knowledge for joint decision-making. Experiments on six benchmarks - ICEWS18, ICEWS14, ICEWS15, GDELT, WIKI and YAGO - demonstrate that FMOGE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving relative improvements of 6.09%, 11.20%, and 12.44% in Hit@K (K = 1, 3, 10) on ICEWS14, confirming its effectiveness in precise event forecasting.

papers.title: Multi-dimensional hierarchical temporal alignment for improved temporal commonsense reasoning in large language models
papers.authors: Ge Y., Yu H.T., Lei C.
papers.abstract: Benefiting from recent advances in generative AI and large language models (LLMs), current LLM-driven AI systems are rapidly reshaping how we reason, plan, and make decisions. Yet endowing these systems with human-like temporal intelligence (e.g., understanding and comparing events across time) remains largely unresolved. To address this gap, we introduce a novel Multi-dimensional Hierarchical Temporal Alignment framework (denoted as MHTA), of which the core idea is to effectively ground the temporal alignment of an LLM in both event-specific and cross-event real-world temporal commonsense knowledge. Specifically, we first frame the temporal space as a multi-dimensional hierarchical space, where each dimension comprises its own set of temporal units. Building on this formulation, we curate an initial burn-in dataset in which annotations are constructed to reflect real-world human temporal commonsense in accordance with our defined temporal space. Based on the initial burn-in dataset, we propose two complementary fine-tuning objectives: (i) Grounding the temporal alignment in event-specific temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved through a novel hierarchy-preserving Wasserstein loss, and (ii) Grounding the temporal alignment in cross-event temporal commonsense knowledge, which is achieved via a margin-adaptive triplet loss. To evaluate the effectiveness of MHTA, we conduct extensive experiments on three representative benchmarks (MCTACO, DurationQA, and TimeDial). For example, on the MCTACO dataset, MHTA improves Mistral-7B by 6.0% in accuracy and 10.3% in exact match, and improves DeepSeek-LLM-7B by 5.4% in accuracy and 9.8% in exact match. Combined with different backbones, MHTA surpasses nearly all baselines across the three benchmarks and exceeds the performance of advanced models such as GPT-4o on MCTACO and DurationQA. These results demonstrate that MHTA provides consistent gains in temporal commonsense reasoning across diverse LLM backbones.

papers.authors: Xun Y., Yan J., Yang H., Cai J., Wang X.

This paper proposes Periodic-Temporal Query Network(PTQNet), a lightweight architecture that explicitly decomposes multi-scale seasonal patterns from residual variations. Two core contributions of PTQNet involve: a hierarchical cycle module that learns data-driven periodic embeddings to capture structured seasonality over a generic bank of candidate cycle lengths and a phase-aware residual attention mechanism that dynamically modulates query representations based on seasonal phase, enabling context-sensitive modeling of non-repeating fluctuations. By jointly optimizing periodic and residual pathways, PTQNet achieves accurate and interpretable forecasts with low computational overhead. Extensive experiments on eight benchmark datasets show that PTQNet outperforms eleven state-of-the-art models, with an average MSE reduction of 15.68% and an average MAE reduction of 14.88% compared to the mean of the 11 baselines. These results demonstrate that PTQNet offers a scalable and practical solution for long-horizon forecasting in resource-constrained environments.

papers.title: Multi-dimensional association scoring and confidence awareness for multimodal cancer survival prediction
papers.authors: Gao G., Zhang K., Hu D., Gan T., Yang J., Rao N.
papers.abstract: Integrating pathology whole-slide images (WSIs) with genomic data for cancer survival prediction holds promise but faces three key challenges: (1) the semantic gap hindering feature alignment; (2) the lack of confidence estimation for individual modality predictions; (3) fusion strategies that neglect reliability differences across modalities. To address these issues, we propose the Multi-dimensional Association Scoring and Confidence Awareness (MASCA) framework. First, we design a multi-dimensional WSI–genomic association scoring mechanism that jointly incorporates semantic similarity, structural matching, and functional attribution to achieve fine-grained alignment between WSI and genomic instance representations. Second, we impose a normal inverse gamma (NIG) prior on the predicted risk scores of all instances to capture both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty of each modality. The NIG distribution is then marginalized to yield a t-distribution, facilitating convenient confidence quantification and cross-modality fusion. Third, we develop a confidence-aware fusion strategy based on the t-distribution that adaptively adjusts fusion weights according to modality-specific confidence levels, thereby improving the reliability of the fused results. Moreover, we devise a confidence ranking regularization term that further enhances the robustness of the fusion process. We evaluated MASCA on five cancer datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), including 2831 survival cases of cancer patients. The results demonstrate that MASCA outperforms state-of-the-art methods, enhancing the C-index by 1.6% and the time-dependent AUC (tAUC) by 2.7%. Therefore, our method can provide more accurate survival predictions for cancer patients, while also assisting clinicians in making effective clinical decisions.

papers.title: Reasoning based on symbolic and parametric knowledge bases: A survey
papers.authors: Xu M., Ning Y., Li Y., Chen J., Wen J., Xiao Y., Zhou S., Pan B., Bao Z., Miao X., Kang H., Sun K., Qian T.
papers.abstract: Reasoning refers to drawing new conclusions based on existing knowledge, which can support various applications. While existing surveys provide comprehensive overviews within their perspectives, they mainly organize methods by task, algorithmic paradigm, or application scenario. As a result, they offer limited discussion and explanation on how the types, properties, and scales of the underlying knowledge bases constrain or strength different reasoning strategies. To bridge this gap, this survey summarizes reasoning methods from the view of their dependent knowledge base. First, this perspective covers a broader range of knowledge bases than previous surveys. This allows for a more comprehensive comparison and understanding of their differences when employed in reasoning. Second, this perspective introduces a data-centric taxonomy that directly reflecting how the distinct characteristics of knowledge bases, such as information density and representational nature, explicitly constrain or enhance reasoning strategies. For instance, high-stakes systems require transparent and verifiable knowledge bases, whereas creative applications prioritize flexibility. Finally, this perspective outlines future directions to guide more advanced reasoning research. It advocates for shifting the focus from purely performance toward more comprehensive metrics such as verifiability, consistency, transparency, and safety

papers.title: Attention Is All We Need: Collaborative Filtering Transformer
papers.authors: Luo J., Mu C., Liu Y., Chen Y.
papers.abstract: Graph encoding and the attention mechanism enable Graph Transformers (GTs) to extract features of graph structures. However, employing graph encoding and Transformer-based attention mechanism may lead to two defects: high computing complexity and sensitivity to graph structures. Therefore, this paper designs a graph feature extractor with a pure or lightweight attention mechanism that does not rely on graph encoding or feature projection matrices, called Collaborative Filtering Transformer (CFT). CFT uses the pure attention mechanism as the main structure of the encoder and introduces non-interaction information by constructing preference sentences. The core of CFT is that its encoder does not contain any collaborative information, but only plays a role in generating associations between different nodes, so that a node on the graph can notice its non-neighboring nodes. The utilization of collaborative information is only achieved through optimizing the loss function. In addition, through theoretical analysis and experimental verification, we prove that adding path-based graph encoding in CFT has a negative effect on the feature extraction process of the attention mechanism. Furthermore, experiments show that during the optimization process, the proposed pure attention mechanism can always assign higher attention scores to nodes with interactions, while making the attention scores between nodes without interactions approach zero. Finally, our model achieves the best performance when compared with the latest methods on five real-world datasets, and compared to the second-best baseline, the recommendation performance is improved by up to 20.60%. Moreover, CFT achieves considerably high training efficiency across all five datasets, with training time comparable to that of simple matrix factorization-based baselines.

papers.title: Large Language Model Guided Graph Capsule Network with Local-Enhanced Alignment for Fake News Detection
papers.authors: Sun G., Li J., Zhang Z.
papers.abstract: Fake news on social media increasingly employs advanced deceptive strategies such as partial tampering and semantic misleading, which create a camouflaged consistency as it exhibits superficial coherence while harboring deeper inconsistencies. Existing detection methods treat cross-modal consistency as a monolithic concept and apply uniform strategies across all samples, rendering them insensitive to these nuanced deception patterns. To address the above issues, we propose the Large Language Model Guided Graph Capsule Network with Local-Enhanced Alignment (LGCNLA) model, a framework that systematically targets three critical dimensions of deception. First, at the semantic layer, we leverage Large Language Models to generate multi-perspective image-enhanced descriptions and supplement external entities, making implicit misleading cues explicit and providing richer contextual evidence. Second, at the structural layer, we construct a dual-channel heterogeneous graph capsule network whose dynamic routing mechanism preserves and amplifies local anomalous patterns that traditional graph based methods would smooth away. Third, at the distributional layer, we reformulate fake news detection as a hierarchical domain alignment task and introduce Local-Enhanced Maximum Mean Discrepancy, which separately aligns cross-modal distributions for real and fake news by minimizing divergence for authentic content while maximizing it for deceptive content, with locality-aware sensitivity to fine-grained inconsistencies. These three components function synergistically such that semantic enrichment provides the evidence, structural preservation highlights the anomalies, and distributional calibration defines the decision objective, thereby creating a holistic detection system that penetrates the camouflage of advanced deceptive strategies. Extensive experiments on Weibo, PolitiFact, and GossipCop datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods, with accuracy improvements of at least 0.021, 0.029, and 0.036 respectively. Unlike standard fixed-patch Transformers that often smooth over speaker-specific micro-textures, the SWF architecture integrates denoising and feature extraction into a single stage, challenging the traditional decoupled paradigm of speech enhancement and recognition. Using a sample of 1.58 million pre-training instances, the model was evaluated across English (RAVDESS), Arabic (ESD), and stressful (SUSAS) datasets. Results demonstrate significant improvements, with the SWF model achieving 91.01% accuracy in clean conditions and maintaining 88.5% in high-noise cocktail party environments, outperforming state-of-the-art models like WavLM and HuBERT. AFMO integrates modality-specific feature extraction with dual outlier filtering and a simulated-annealing feature-selection module to optimize the fusion of heterogeneous signals. Its main contribution is an adaptive selection mechanism that suppresses cross-modal interference, thereby improving discrimination between authentic and fake content. Experiments on Weibo, GossipCop, and PolitiFact show that AFMO consistently outperforms recent competitive baselines. On Weibo, AFMO achieves 92.23% accuracy, supporting the claim that mitigating cross-modal interference can materially improve veracity prediction.

papers.title: Bridging cross-modalities: Deep learning approaches for sketch-based 3D shape retrieval
papers.authors: Xiang M., Bai J., Gao L., Wang Y., Qin F.
papers.abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized 3D content processing, elevating it to new levels and generating opportunities for intuitive interaction in virtual reality and industrial design. This article surveys the current landscape of Deep Learning-based Sketch-Based 3D Shape Retrieval (SBSR), focusing on its methodological evolution, effectiveness, and transformative impact. Based on a comprehensive review of over 130 studies published since the shift from handcrafted features, we discover that the potential of deep learning is particularly notable in a proposed four-level analytical framework: (1) Data Augmentation, examining sketch-domain techniques covering both non-learnable and learnable methods, as well as 3D shape-domain strategies based on point clouds and multi-view renderings, to mitigate data scarcity and enhance cross-modal consistency; (2) Feature Extraction, examining both static and dynamic (sequential) sketch representations, as well as the optimization of multi-view 3D representations; (3) Feature Alignment, categorizing strategies into unidirectional and bidirectional collaborations to bridge the semantic gap; and (4) Feature Matching, discussing metric learning advancements. Furthermore, by analyzing performance trends on key benchmarks (e.g., SHREC’13, SHREC’14), we highlight how the emergence of dynamic sketch modeling and the adoption of advanced multi-view 3D fusion strategies have significantly advanced the state-of-the-art. We conclude by emphasizing emerging frontiers—such as fine-grained, zero-shot, and scene-level retrieval. Finally, we introduces derivative tasks related to SBSR, discusses the key challenges faced by the research community, and proposes directions for future work.

papers.title: Noise-robust item modeling and dynamic multiview contrastive learning for multimodal recommendation
papers.authors: Gong Z.H., Wang J.W., Hu P., Dong M., Li Y.M., Li Z.F., Zhang Y., Zhang M.
papers.abstract: Multimodal recommender systems enhance recommendation accuracy by leveraging multimodal item information together with users’ interaction histories. Existing methods mainly use item–item semantic graphs and user–item interaction graphs to model item and user preferences. However, in item modeling, existing methods often overlook collaborative relationships between items, which makes it difficult to capture comprehensive item features. On the interaction side, they treat all interactions as equally reliable, overlooking differences across behavior types and their varying importance to users. To address these issues, we propose Noise-Robust Item Modeling and Dynamic Multiview Contrastive Learning (NRDMC), a novel method for multimodal recommendation. First, we extract latent collaborative signals between items from user–item interactions to enhance comprehensive modeling of item features. Second, we design intra-modal and cross-modal attention mechanisms. The intra-modal attention suppresses noise within each modality, while the cross-modal attention exploits complementary information across modalities. Finally, NRDMC adopts dynamic multi-view contrastive learning to capture latent behavior prototypes and their importance in user–item interactions. This enables the model to construct higher-quality contrastive views and improve recommendation performance. To ensure fair comparison, we evaluate NRDMC on three public Amazon Reviews benchmark datasets (Baby, Sports, and Clothing) under standard settings. Experimental results show that NRDMC consistently outperforms strong baselines, achieving average performance gains of 3.49%, 7.54%, and 1.64% on Baby, Sports, and Clothing, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/50hehe/NRDMC.

papers.title: PhiMark: watermarking relational data robustly with zero distortion
papers.authors: Ji J., Peng Y., Ma W., Li H., Cui J., Gao X.
papers.abstract: AbstractRelational data is vulnerable to copyright infringement during data transactions. Robust database watermarking is an effective approach to protect data copyright. However, existing schemes embed watermarks by altering the original data, which inevitably compromises data utility and restricts their applicability in high-accuracy applications (i.e., governmental applications, medical applications, etc.). To address these issues, a zero-distortion robust database watermarking scheme (PhiMark) is proposed by employing a novel partition-and-mask approach. Specifically, a hash function is used to partition the original data, and a mask is generated for each partition based on extracted features. A genetic algorithm is introduced to automatically optimize the watermark parameters to reduce the manual efforts involved in parameter tuning. Subsequently, the verification evidence is derived by calculating the mask and watermark (i.e., copyright information) and stored for watermark extraction. PhiMark is a promising approach to both support digital asset protection and maintain the protected database unchanged. Additionally, it is compatible with both textual and numerical data, while existing schemes are tailored for either one. These features significantly enhance its potential for practical deployment. Experimental evaluations on real-world datasets demonstrate the superior robustness of PhiMark over state-of-the-art schemes. Specifically, on a dataset with tens of millions of tuples, watermark embedding requires only 84 seconds, and the average accuracy of watermark extraction remains at 94.3% under common malicious attacks (such as deletion, alteration, etc.) with a 95% attack ratio, which is 12.6% higher than the existing optimal scheme.

papers.title: Distributed semantic trajectory similarity join
papers.authors: Tian R., Hou Y., Gao S., Alenezi F., Polat K.
papers.abstract: Similarity join is a fundamental operation for managing semantic trajectory data. In massive data scenarios, distributed paradigms can be utilized to process similarity joins for huge amounts of semantic trajectory data, but they face the challenge of locally aware partitioning of the data. To address this problem, we propose a distributed similarity join framework based on trajectory segments. The semantic trajectory data are partitioned by segments, and semantically similar trajectories are stored in the same partition to improve the local similarity of the partitions. We design global and local indexes to efficiently manage partitioned data. We develop a filtering validation framework to enhance similarity query performance by pruning irrelevant trajectories based on the temporal, spatial, and semantic distances of trajectory segments. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior scalability and query efficiency, compared to other methods.

papers.title: A dual-source knowledge distillation framework for hate speech detection based on cognitive distortion awareness
papers.authors: Li C., Zhang M.
papers.abstract: AbstractTraditional hate speech detection methods primarily focus on surface-level semantic cues and emotional intensity, resulting in suboptimal performance when identifying implicit and complex hate speech. To address this challenge, this study introduces cognitive distortion as an actionable reasoning cue and proposes a Cognitive Distortion-Aware Dual-Source Knowledge Distillation (CDA-DKD) framework. The framework employs a two-stage strategy. First, an Expert-Guided Cognitive Amplification (EGCA) mechanism is designed to enrich sparse signals and resolve ambiguous boundaries associated with cognitive distortions in training data. Second, a Dual-Teacher Single-Student Dual-Source Knowledge Distillation (DSKD) architecture is constructed. This architecture efficiently distills knowledge from two specialized expert teachers—one focusing on semantics and the other on cognitive distortions—into a lightweight student model. Evaluated on three public datasets (IHC, SBIC, and DYNA), the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art Macro F1-scores of 79.73%, 91.34%, and 84.25%, respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that CDA-DKD significantly improves detection robustness, particularly in identifying implicit hate speech devoid of explicit offensive vocabulary.

papers.title: MedCTM: A CNN-Transformer-Mamba Hybrid Network for Medical Image Classification
papers.authors: Pan W., Kang J., Wang X., Lv C., Zhang X., Liu X.
papers.abstract: Medical image classification requires models that jointly capture local textures and long-range dependencies, while remaining efficient enough for practical use. To meet these requirements, we propose MedCTM, a CNN-Transformer-Mamba hybrid network. It decomposes feature learning into three complementary branches: local feature extraction, long-range dependency modeling, and cross-branch interaction. The core of MedCTM is the Bidirectional Channel Interaction Attention (BCIA) module. This module enables dynamic information exchange between CNN and Mamba features by allowing each to condition the other. A three-stage cascade is then used to progressively refine multi-scale representations. We evaluate MedCTM on eight medical image datasets that span seven modalities and over 100,000 samples. The model achieves strong performance with only 1.42-2.63 GFLOPs. On the average F1 score across the eight datasets, MedCTM outperforms the state-of-the-art MedViTv2 by 0.5%–1.7%, while using 12.9%–24.4% fewer parameters.

papers.title: AmanNet: Adaptive multi-window and adversarial noise network for volatile time series prediction
papers.authors: Shen L., Chen M., Liu C., Sun W., Li S., Li Z.
papers.abstract: Volatile time series is characterized by significant uncertainty and fluctuations, posing significant challenges for accurate prediction. Existing approaches often face two major limitations: (1) the difficulty of modeling both long-term and short-term patterns using their fixed-length input strategies, and (2) the susceptibility to overfitting and poor generalization due to the data scarcity and high noise. To address these issues, we propose Adatpvie multi-window and adversarial noise Network (AmanNet), a novel framework with two key innovations: (1) adaptive multi-window networks that process input via variable and learnable look-back window lengths, enabling dynamic capture of multi-scale temporal patterns, and (2) adaptive adversarial noise that injects adversarial noise with varying intensities across multi-window networks, thereby enhancing model robustness. Evaluated on seven real-world datasets of cryptocurrencies and stock price sequences, AmanNet achieves accuracy improvements of 4.3–8.1% and MCC gains of 19.3–55.2% over state-of-the-art models, under both 1-day and 3-day predictions. These results demonstrate AmanNet’s effectiveness in modeling volatile, noisy time series with superior generalization and robustness. Code is available in https://anonymous.4open.science/r/AmanNet_IPM26-1.

papers.title: Predicting tourism product advertising effectiveness: Fusing multimodal large language models with visually-rich document understanding
papers.authors: Chen R., Xiao J., Yang Z., Yang H., Yang J.
papers.abstract: With the advent of generative artificial intelligence (AI), which has drastically reduced the cost of content generation, the design of visual and textual advertising for online tourism products has gained new significance. However, how to design effective multimodal advertising remains underexplored. Prior research has shown that such advertising influences consumer decisions, yet few studies have extracted hierarchical visual cues in an interpretable manner and have quantified their predictive value for promotional outcomes. We propose a multimodal prediction framework based on a multimodal large language model (MLLM) for tourism advertising effectiveness. The framework extracts visual structural cues with LayoutXLM and abstract visual content cues with an MLLM, then fuses them via a dual-gated module to predict advertising effectiveness, providing quantitative support for evaluation and deployment. We conducted experiments on 8640 products collected from Ctrip over a period of five months. The results indicated that fusing visual structural features and content features enabled the model to achieve the best performance. Compared with the baseline, the MSE decreased by 0.2396. The RMSE decreased by 0.1280. The R² increased by 0.1541. This study provides merchants with practical guidance on advertising design and offers online travel platforms data-driven strategies for advertising placement.

papers.title: A distributed quantization mechanism for lightweight federated learning model in heterogeneous on-device AI networks
papers.authors: Bibi M., Khan Q.W., Yazdan S.A., Ahmad R., Kim D.H.
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed devices while preserving data privacy, yet its practical deployment remains constrained by communication bottlenecks, hardware heterogeneity, and limited bandwidth. This study introduces Quantization-aware Federated Learning (QFL), a dual-sided quantization framework designed to enhance communication efficiency and scalability in resource-constrained environments. QFL integrates 4-bit and 8-bit QSGD to compress model updates symmetrically at both client and server sides, forming a bidirectional compression pipeline that optimizes uplink and downlink communication without compromising convergence stability. Comprehensive experiments conducted on the MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, real-world Diabetes and Mortality Prediction datasets validate QFL’s robustness across diverse data distributions and hardware configurations. The framework achieves up to 87.5% model compression with less than 2% accuracy degradation, while reducing ATT by 29% and RTT by 43% compared to full-precision baselines. Theoretical analysis further establishes QFL’s unbiased gradient estimation and bounded quantization variance, confirming convergence equivalence.QFL demonstrates strong applicability for real-time, privacy-preserving FL in heterogeneous edge environments, particularly in healthcare, IoT, and intelligent industrial systems, offering a scalable, energy-efficient foundation for next-generation distributed intelligence.

papers.title: LSFL: A Lightweight and Secure Federated Learning scheme for Internet of Vehicles
papers.authors: Wei L., Peng D., Shi Y., Shi L., Li G., Lian H.
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) presents a privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative training in Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environments. Its IoV deployment introduces security vulnerabilities requiring systematic mitigation, with a pivotal challenge being adversarial crafting of malicious model updates that compromise global model integrity and functional performance, while adversaries may also exploit gradient leakage to reconstruct sensitive private data, exacerbating IoV privacy concerns. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Lightweight and Secure Federated Learning (LSFL) scheme for IoV, where LSFL specifically incorporates a robust cosine similarity based aggregation mechanism to identify and filter malicious updates for countering poisoning attacks, further integrates lightweight homomorphic encryption to safeguard gradient confidentiality and mitigate private data reconstruction risks, and takes minimizing overhead as a core objective to ensure compatibility with resource-constrained IoV edge devices. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets and models show that LSFL significantly enhances model robustness against poisoning attacks, effectively prevents privacy reconstruction from gradients, and reduces encryption overhead compared to baseline methods. This provides a practical and secure solution for privacy-preserving federated learning in Internet of Vehicles.

papers.title: Dynamic weighted knowledge distillation for skin lesion diagnosis
papers.authors: Liu P., Zhang H., Qian W.
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers an effective strategy for skin cancer diagnosis, enabling efficient model deployment in resource-constrained clinical environments while maintaining high diagnostic accuracy. Although existing methods for mitigating logit collapse have shown promise, they often fail to capture the intrinsic relationships among non-target classes, thereby limiting effective knowledge transfer, especially in skin cancer diagnosis where similar lesions require capturing inter-class relationships. To address the problem, we propose Dynamic Weighted Knowledge Distillation (DWKD), a novel framework that constructs a sample-wise weighting mechanism based on the normalized prediction entropy of the teacher model. This mechanism dynamically balances two key knowledge: logit knowledge and inter-non-target-class relational knowledge extracted from skin lesion feature representations. By adaptively regulating the distillation process, DWKD effectively alleviates the limitations of non-target class knowledge transfer caused by logit collapse in conventional methods. We conducted extensive experiments on two large-scale, publicly available skin lesion datasets, where DWKD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art knowledge distillation methods, achieving 88.5% accuracy on ISIC 2019 and 91.0% on ISIC 2018.

papers.title: A dual-level indicative representation learning method for multimodal sarcasm detection
papers.authors: Zhang Y., Su G., Wang T., Wu M., Wei X.
papers.abstract: Multimodal sarcasm detection is essential for enhancing interpersonal understanding and communication, particularly in social media analysis and human–computer interaction. However, while existing methods effectively integrate deep features from multimodal information, they often neglect the semantic contrast between literal expression and underlying intent. This contrast arises from the implicit meanings of specific elements within a single modality, as well as the descriptive contradictions that emerge between elements across different modalities. To address this challenge, we formalize contrast characterization as a problem of indicative representation learning and propose a Dual-level Indicative Representation Learning Method (DIRLM), which is designed to explicitly capture these sarcastic elements. Specifically, to explore intra-modality contrast, DIRLM incorporates a supervised module that employs counterfactual reasoning to identify key indicative features across diverse contextual scenarios. To further leverage inter-modality contrast, the method introduces an unsupervised projection module based on orthogonal mapping, which enhances cross-modal coherence by suppressing non-indicative features while amplifying indicative ones. To validate the effectiveness of our proposed method, we conducted comprehensive experiments on two widely-used real-world datasets, MMSD and MMSD2.0. Our method achieved an accuracy of 88.98% on the MMSD2.0 dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin of at least 2.16%.

papers.title: SocLitGen: An LLM-assisted framework for automated literature review in social sciences
papers.authors: Hu S., Wei Y., Sun S.
papers.abstract: Existing automated literature review technologies primarily target computer science contexts and face significant adaptability challenges in social science disciplines. Addressing this gap, this study proposes SocLitGen, a seven-module framework specifically designed for social science literature review generation. SocLitGen was evaluated using review tasks from management and economics topics on a corpus of 1,559,141 papers, comparing against Naive RAG, AutoSurvey, and graduate student writing. Baseline comparisons show that in citation quality (recall and precision), SocLitGen outperforms Naive RAG by at least 39.9%; in content quality (academic professionalism, structural rationality, and language fluency), SocLitGen outperforms AutoSurvey by at least 13.1% and graduate student writing by at least 9.5%. Cross-context evaluations reveal differentiated performance patterns: cross-disciplinary analysis confirms consistent performance across management and economics; cross-model experiments show Qwen2.5 performs optimally in academic and structural dimensions while GLM-4 excels in language fluency; cross-literature scale analysis demonstrates that large-scale sets enhance professionalism and structure but reduce fluency.

papers.title: Robust image steganography without modification based on co-occurrence labels
papers.authors: Liu Y., Luo X., Zhang M., Fan W., Zhang Y.
papers.abstract: Most existing image steganography without modification (SWM) methods leverage stable features for covert transmission that resist common channel attacks. However, their limited feature space restricts hiding capacity. To this end, we propose a robust SWM method based on co-occurrence labels (CooL-SWM). It exploits both the semantic stability and co-occurrence patterns of object category labels. Specifically, CooL-SWM extracts co-occurrence features from natural images and constructs co-occurrence matrices through label permutations, expanding the feature space. By using unique spatial positions, CooL-SWM establishes a bijective mapping between secret messages and co-occurrence features. This improves feature space utilization and hiding capacity. We also introduce a structured text prompt template and a label-to-image semantic consistency strategy. These ensure the generated stego images strictly match the co-occurrence label sequences, improving hiding success rate and extraction accuracy. Different from existing object-based SWM methods, CooL-SWM requires no auxiliary information such as the number of stego objects per transmission, obviating additional transmission risks. Experimental results based on VOC2012 and COCO2014 demonstrate that, while ensuring complete hiding of secret messages, the proposed CooL-SWM achieves 1.75 times and 2.33 times higher hiding capacity compared with existing object-based SWM methods, with average extraction accuracy improvements of 23.48% and 30.59%, respectively, showcasing its application prospects in real-world lossy network channels.

papers.title: A Domain-Adapted Pipeline for Structured Information Extraction from Police Incident Announcements on Social Media
papers.authors: Shen M., Song K., Wang X., Jia W., Wang T., Han Z.
papers.abstract: Structured information extraction from police incident announcements is crucial for timely, accurate data processing, yet it poses considerable challenges due to the variability and informal nature of textual sources such as social media posts. To address these challenges, we developed a domain-adapted extraction pipeline that leverages targeted prompt engineering with parameter-efficient fine-tuning of the Qwen2.5–7B model using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). This approach enables the model to handle noisy, heterogeneous text while reliably extracting 15 key fields, including location, event characteristics, and impact assessment, from a high-quality, manually annotated dataset of 4933 instances derived from 27,822 police briefing posts on Chinese Weibo (2019–2020). Experimental results demonstrated that LoRA-based fine-tuning significantly improved performance over both the base and instruction-tuned models, achieving an accuracy exceeding 98.36% for mortality detection and Exact Match Rates of 95.31% for fatality counts and 95.54% for province-level location extraction. The proposed pipeline thus provides a validated and efficient solution for multi-task structured information extraction in specialized domains, offering a practical framework for transforming unstructured text into reliable structured data in social science research.

papers.title: From Perception to Comprehension: A cognitive hierarchy for multimodal relation extraction
papers.authors: Meng Z., Zhao M., Xu T., Yu J., Yu R., He Y., Yu M.
papers.abstract: Human comprehension of multimodal information follows a hierarchical cognitive process that evolves from perception to integrated understanding. Inspired by this mechanism, we reinterpret multi-modal relation extraction (MRE) as a cognitive progression rather than a flat feature fusion task as in the existing methods. We propose a Cognitive Hierarchy Framework (CHF) that models multimodal reasoning through sequential stages: perception, association, reasoning, self-regulation and comprehension. Each stage incrementally aligns and refines cross-modal representations, leading to interpretable and efficient relational understanding without incorporating external structured knowledge or explicit relational supervision. Experiments on two datasets show that CHF achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving F1 by 2.37% on MNRE and 1.25% on MORE, while reducing fusion parameters by 62%. Ablation and visualization analyses further demonstrate how cross-modal consistency is gradually established across stages. These results suggest that incorporating hierarchical cognitive principles provides a promising direction for human-like multimodal reasoning.

papers.title: SADET: Efficient active suspension control for intensive care ambulances via self-attention and deterministic experience tracking
papers.authors: He X., Liu J., Meng Y., Lin H.
papers.abstract: High-dimensional vibration control in intensive care ambulances demands algorithms that are simultaneously high-performance and lightweight for real-world deployment. This study proposes the SADET algorithm, which integrates a Self-Attention (SA) mechanism with Deterministic Experience Tracking (DET) within an asymmetric strong Critic and weak Actor architecture. Built upon a 7-DOF ambulance dynamics model and a domain-randomization training protocol over ISO 8608 random road profiles, the SA-enhanced Critic enables an extremely lightweight Actor, with the derived SADET-n requiring only 124 parameters, representing a 99.9 % reduction from the DET baseline. Experimental results demonstrate that the top-performing SADET-x variant achieves vertical vibration suppression improvements of 62.9 %, 56.4 %, and 11.0 % over DDPG, TD3, and DET respectively, while reducing the root mean square values of roll and pitch accelerations by 75.4 % and 56.5 %. Generalization studies on 400 unseen road profiles spanning Classes A through D, vehicle speeds from 10 to 50 m/s, and sprung mass variations of ±500 kg confirm robust cross-scenario adaptability, and dedicated fault-injection tests further verify that performance is sustained under sensor noise and intermittent data loss representative of production automotive sensor networks. Comparative power analysis additionally shows that SADET delivers state-of-the-art comfort improvement at an actuator power consumption no higher than that of substantially less effective baselines. The present work establishes a deployable lightweight framework for the application of deep reinforcement learning to complex real-world control systems and provides a meaningful advance in the safety and comfort of medical transportation.

papers.title: Disentangling generative chaos: A multi-scale hypergraph diffusion framework for interpretable recommendation
papers.authors: Tuo S., Geng J., Chen S., Qiu K., Luo Z.
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation often suffers from “generative chaos”—a disordered and entangled latent state that degrades ranking accuracy and interpretability. To address this challenge, we propose Dis-Rec, a framework that pioneers a “structure-guided generation” paradigm. Dis-Rec operates through three synergistic components: (1) utilizing a latent diffusion model to construct a high-fidelity user preference manifold, providing a robust informational foundation; (2) introducing a multi-scale hypergraph strategy to concurrently encode short-term sequential contexts and long-term interest patterns into a unified structural prior; and (3) devising a disentangled gating decoder that exploits these topological priors to steer the automatic decomposition of chaotic latent vectors into semantically orthogonal intent channels, enabling context-aware adaptive fusion via a dynamic gating mechanism. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate significant performance gains. Notably, compared with the strongest baseline, Dis-Rec achieves a 7.67% relative improvement in NDCG@10 on ML-1 M and a 4.24% Recall gain on the sparse Toys dataset, effectively overcoming the data scarcity bottleneck typical of generative models. These results verify the critical role of structured disentanglement in enhancing the robustness of generative recommendation.

papers.title: TemFRC: Enterprise financial risk prediction with temporal folding and risk contrast
papers.authors: Wang M., Huang W., Xie W., Hou J., Gao X., Fu X.
papers.abstract: AbstractEnterprise financial risk prediction constitutes a critical component of contemporary corporate governance, profoundly impacting an organization’s capacity for risk mitigation and data-driven decision-making. However, existing methods that treat financial data as a time series mostly focus on capturing trend variations, while ignoring the fact that enterprise development often exhibits periodic patterns and inter-enterprise similarities, resulting in limited model capacity to learn financial characteristics. To address this issue, we propose TemFRC, a novel method for enterprise financial risk prediction that enhances model performance by capturing various periodic patterns in financial data and leveraging risk similarity among enterprises. Specifically, TemFRC consists of two core modules: the temporal folding module and the risk contrast module. The temporal folding module transforms one-dimensional time series into two-dimensional temporal feature maps, enabling more comprehensive capture of trend variations and periodic patterns in financial data. The risk contrast module optimizes enterprise feature representations within the embedding space via contrastive learning, thereby facilitating the modeling of inter-enterprise risk similarities. Finally, the feature representations learned through the two modules are leveraged to determine whether a company is at risk of financial distress. Experiments are conducted on a real-world financial statement dataset comprising 3622 listed companies. The results demonstrate that TemFRC achieves state-of-the-art prediction performance, reaching a Macro-F1 score of 0.8753, which represents a 2.87% improvement over the best-performing baseline model.

papers.title: Diffusion-based generative modeling for expert team formation
papers.authors: Saliminabi M.H., Ebrahimi S., Hamidi Rad R., Androutsos D., Zarrinkalam F., Bagheri E.
papers.abstract: Forming effective expert teams is central to domains where solving complex problems requires diverse, complementary skills. However, automating this task is highly challenging due to sparse co-occurrence data, long-tailed expert participation, and the combinatorial complexity of unseen skill configurations. Existing graph-based, probabilistic, and neural approaches often struggle with generalization, fairness, and robustness, leading to biased selections that favor historically popular experts over more suitable candidates. To address these challenges, we propose a generative framework for expert team formation based on denoising diffusion probabilistic models. We cast team formation as skill-conditioned imputation (i.e., inpainting), where skills are treated as observed context and the expert component is generated via conditional diffusion sampling. This design enables our method to preserve semantic skill–expert alignment, mitigate data sparsity, and generate diverse yet contextually coherent teams. Extensive experiments on DBLP and DOTA2 datasets show that our model consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving over 3× higher recall (16.4% vs. 5.0%) and MAP (9.7% vs. 2.2%) on DBLP, while delivering more than 5× improvement in MRR (13.3% vs. 2.5%) on DOTA2. Fairness analysis further demonstrates that our method reduces average overlap with the top-100 most popular experts to 2.6, compared to 86.7 for the strongest baseline, and achieves near-optimal diversity with NDKL ≈ 0.1 under high non-popular expert ratios.For reproducibility purposes, we made our code and model publicly available at https://github.com/17shiraz/DiffTF.

papers.title: Structure-aware multi-teacher distillation for noise node classification
papers.authors: Hu B., Wen G., Huang Y., Liu Y., Zhu X.
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation methods are very popular for solving the issue of noise node classification (NNC). However, these methods often fail to consider the structural information in graph data or output uncorrected prediction labels in the teacher models due to the influence of noise labels, resulting in degraded generalization performance for constructing a teacher–student training framework in the Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). To effectively address this challenge, we propose a new method named Structure-Aware Multi-Teacher Distillation (SAMTD) for noise node classification. Specifically, we first train multiple teacher models to ensure diversity. We then propose an embedding structure consistency distillation method to make the student model capture the rich structural information encoded in the teachers’ embeddings, as well as a prediction consistency weighting strategy to guide the student model to focus more on the reliable classification knowledge provided by the teacher models. Finally, we introduce a label enhancement module to continuously improve the overall label quality in the dataset. Experimental results on five real-world datasets under five different noise settings demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods in classification accuracy, achieving an average improvement of 1.2%. papers.title: An LLM-based NLP pipeline to assist government agencies in digesting massive public comments and mitigating spam
papers.authors: Dong W., Zhu R., Jensen M., Bessarabova E., Sachdeva S., Kim J.N., Talbert N., Perez L.A., Li Y.
papers.abstract: Public comments are a crucial resource for regulatory agencies in policy-making. However, large-scale comment analysis is labor-intensive and heavily distorted by spam. While large language models (LLMs) present a promising solution, real-world deployments face critical challenges, including spam-biased topic distribution and argument-extraction errors. Moreover, several agencies we interviewed treat data privacy as one of their top priorities, hence restricting the use of cloud-based LLMs. Meanwhile, the effectiveness of privacy-preserving local models remains underexplored in rule-making. This study aims to develop a unified LLM-based summarization pipeline that jointly quantifies spam volume, detects spam templates, and enables argument-aware summarization, while remaining deployable under real-world privacy constraints. We conduct experiments on three public comment datasets drawn from the Federal Communications Commission, the Forest Service, and the Department of Labor’s Wage and Hour Division in collaboration with communication experts and government staff. The results reveal that the proposed pipeline achieves promising performance on quantifying spam volume, with an F1 score of 0.987, 0.993, and 0.995. The pipeline further addresses spam template detection, consistently achieving a high BERTScore when compared with expert-defined ground-truth templates. We also evaluate the pipeline’s performance on argument-aware summarization, finding that few-shot prompting notably outperforms its zero-shot counterparts. When implemented locally in Llama, a much smaller version of the LLM, the pipeline performed comparably to GPT-4, the state-of-the-art cloud-based LLM. papers.title: MSTDF-AD: Modeling spatiotemporal dependency fusion for non-stationary time series anomaly detection

This paper proposes a novel modeling spatiotemporal dependency fusion for non-stationary time series anomaly detection (MSTDF-AD), featuring three key innovations: (1) Spatiotemporal fusion decomposition: Jointly models complex dependencies while extracting stable components; (2) Multiscale feature fusion: Integrates cross-scale information to enhance local–global anomaly perception; (3) Dynamic KL divergence weight: Using simulated annealing to adaptively optimize VAE training, mitigating posterior collapse. Evaluated on five real-world datasets, industrial control (SWaT), cloud services (PSM), hardware maintenance (SMD), and aerospace monitoring (MSL/SMAP), MSTDF-AD achieves a 96.47% average F1-score, outperforming 19 baseline methods (e.g., +2.58% over GDCMAD, +0.21% over MtsCID), with exceptional performance in hardware fault detection (SMD: 93.94%) and spacecraft telemetry (SMAP: 97.85%), validating its effectiveness in anomaly detection tasks. papers.title: Dynamic knowledge landscape construction for AI-driven emergency decision-making: An STM-LLM framework with triple-LLM synergistic labeling
papers.authors: He K., Wu J., Wang C.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance emergency decision-making, but systematic reviews of its knowledge evolution remain lacking. Based on 525 papers on AI-driven emergency decision-making (AI-EDM) from Web of Science (2020–2025), this study proposes an STM-LLM framework integrating Structural Topic Modeling (STM) and Large Language Models (LLMs), and develops a Triple-LLM Synergistic Labeling (TLS) mechanism for automated and bias-resistant topic labeling generation. To validate the efficacy of the framework, systematic comparative and ablation experiments were designed. The application of the framework in the field of AI-EDM facilitates the identification of research topics, followed by analysis of their spatiotemporal distribution and evolution. A Logistic-Normal Generalized Linear Model (GLM) quantified the effects of five covariates on topic prevalence, and a three-dimensional strategic map identified research frontiers and gaps. The experimental results show that the STM-LLM framework significantly outperforms mainstream baseline methods in both topic label quality and generation efficiency, and the TLS mechanism effectively improves labeling stability. The study identified nine stable topics in the AI-EDM domain that show a “growth-consolidation-decline” pattern. Research funding showed a positive correlation with the development of human–AI collaborative platforms ((Formula presented) ), and differences in research focus were observed between Chinese and international scholars. None of the topics demonstrated significant preferences in terms of collaboration type. Both human intervention and type of decision objective demonstrated distinct patterns of association with different topics. Furthermore, Topics are categorized into four types—Leading, Emerging, Receding, and Persistent. Based on these findings, we further propose a “problem–technology–benefit” framework to systematically support domain advancement. The STM-LLM framework automates dynamic knowledge landscape construction, overcoming manual topic labeling limitations and offering data-driven methodological and practical support for AI-EDM research.

papers.title: S2RAF: A Semantic and Structure aware ReAsoning Framework for question answering over textual graphs
papers.authors: Luo J., Hu P., Zhang M.
papers.abstract: Textual graph question answering (Graph QA) aims to answer natural language queries by reasoning over graphs with textual attributes. Existing methods typically introduce secondary or noisy information when retrieving question-relevant subgraphs. Moreover, the information gap between graph structure and semantics often results in information loss, negatively impacting model performance. In this paper, we propose a Semantic and Structure aware ReAsoning Framework (S2RAF), which integrates structural and semantic information for precise retrieval of relevant facts and high-quality injection of reasoning knowledge. Specifically, we first develop a question-guided retrieval mechanism to dynamically adjust node weights for the adaptive extraction of targeted subgraphs. Then, a dual-level optimization strategy is introduced, combining an LLM-based reasoning scorer with a similarity-based semantic scorer to jointly optimize the subgraphs, effectively denoising and focusing on critical facts. Finally, we propose G-Adapter, which dynamically injects graph information into LLMs, achieving graph-text fusion and enhancing reasoning ability over graphs. Extensive experiments on four Graph QA datasets demonstrate that S2RAF successfully achieves competitive performance. Particularly, S2RAF outperforms existing methods by 5.63%, 5.36%, and 23.83% on ExplaGraphs, SceneGraphs, and CWQ datasets, respectively, confirming the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed model.

papers.title: Large language models for business and management applications: A review
papers.authors: Arslan M., Munawar S., Riaz Z., Cruz C.
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly reshaping business and management, yet existing reviews remain fragmented, with limited integration of bibliometric structure and operational insights. This study addresses that gap by combining bibliometric analysis with a systematic thematic synthesis, linking publication trends, intellectual structure, and real-world deployment patterns across 84 application-focused studies selected from an initial pool of 210 records identified from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (up to August 2025). The analysis shows a sharp post-2023 expansion of research alongside a shift from general-purpose conversational use toward domain-specific and architecture-aware implementations. In contrast to prior reviews, this study identifies how application patterns differ across domains: knowledge-intensive contexts increasingly adopt retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for grounding, while finance applications more frequently rely on fine-tuned and domain-specific models. Keyword co-occurrence analysis highlights a technology-centric core, dominated by ChatGPT, foundation models, and RAG, linked to key business domains including operations, finance, marketing, and supply chain management. While organisations are increasingly adopting customised LLM pipelines and governance-aware workflows, challenges persist in accuracy, integration, ethical risk, and data quality. By consolidating dispersed evidence, this study offers a structured understanding of emerging application patterns and provides guidance for future research and responsible enterprise adoption of LLMs.

papers.title: Exploring contextual and pairwise semantic-enhanced embedding with adaptive fusion for knowledge graph completion
papers.authors: Xue Z., Chen J., Hu X., Lin Z.
papers.abstract: Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) aims to predict missing facts by embedding entities and relations, emerging as the predominant method for intelligent reasoning. However, existing KGC approaches tend to ignore the potential noise and uncertainty, as the contribution of each connected relation to entities varies across distinct link scenarios. Moreover, the simple aggregation process during embedding learning struggles to capture both global and local information simultaneously. To overcome these issues, this paper proposes the Adaptive Contextual-Pairwise Network (AdaCPN) model. Specifically, hybrid-granularity semantic augmentation derives a contextual representation of triplets by attending to the surrounding feature information, and suppressing redundant semantic information. Furthermore, it boosts predictive semantics with pairwise frequency weights of triplets, achieving dynamic contribution allocation and alleviating semantic distribution disparity. Additionally, AdaCPN utilizes adaptive convolution kernels of distinct sizes to broaden the receptive field, which fuses global and detailed features during the aggregation process. AdaCPN is validated on nine benchmark datasets, containing millions of triplets. Experimental results confirm that in MRR on FB15k-237 and WN18RR, AdaCPN not only outperforms neural network-based SOTA methods with improvements of 5.8% and 3.4% (0.430 vs. 0.372, 0.551 vs. 0.517), but also improves by 3.8% and 0.2% (0.430 vs. 0.392, 0.551 vs. 0.549) compared to LLM-based SOTA approaches.

papers.title: Semi-COPRA: An overlapping community-aware model for multi-dimensional opinion dynamics and consensus analysis

papers.abstract: The evolution of group opinions in social networks is fundamentally shaped by community structure, particularly in networks with overlapping communities and multi-dimensional opinions. Experiments on four real-world networks demonstrate that Semi-COPRA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, yielding average improvements of 81% in EQ, 15% in F1 score, and 27% in ONMI over the original COPRA. Simulation results show that increasing community overlap enhances inter-group consensus while weakening intra-group cohesion. In addition, moderate topic interdependence accelerates convergence across opinion dimensions, facilitating the formation of global consensus. These findings establish a structurally integrated modeling framework that links overlapping community detection with multi-dimensional opinion evolution, providing new insights into information diffusion and opinion regulation in complex social systems.

papers.title: Modelling implicit bias in gender–career associations: A systematic comparison of language models
papers.authors: Porshnev A., Kiy K.D., O'Donoghue D., Singh M., Wingfield C., Lynott D.
papers.abstract: Biases in language and their reflection in language models have attracted researchers' attention, particularly with the growth of large language models (LLMs). However, many questions on the links between language models and people’s biased attitudes remain unanswered. In the current preregistered study, we focus on gender–career bias to examine the extent to which language models can be used to model behavioural responses in the Gender–Career Implicit Association Test (IAT). We provide a systematic evaluation of a range of language models, including n-gram, count vector, predict (word2vec), and Large Language Models (LLMs), to determine how well they capture people’s behaviour in the IAT. We compared response time data from over 800,000 participants from the UK and US against 25 language models, with a total of 675 model variants. We find that many language models, including large language models (LLMs), correlated well with human behavior. While results support previous findings for both predict and count model families, we observed that performance of LLMs was consistently different from that of simpler predict models, frequently exhibiting correlations in the opposite direction. Thus, our findings reinforce the idea that societal biases are generally encoded in language, but that large language models can exhibit behaviors different to classical language models. papers.title: A comprehensive review of Artificial Intelligence in Qur’anic research: Trends, methods, challenges, and future directions
papers.authors: Al-Azani S., Abudalfa S., Samma H.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a transformative tool in the Holy Qur’an domain, supporting diverse tasks including recitation accuracy assessment (e.g., Tajweed rule detection), semantic exegesis (e.g., contextual retrieval of Tafsir), verse classification (e.g., identifying rulings or themes), and memorization support (e.g., providing feedback on recitation accuracy). However, applying AI in the domain of the Holy Qur’an requires prioritizing religious principles and ensuring a high level of accuracy in accordance with those principles. This study provides a comprehensive review of the role of AI in Qur’anic research, based on an analysis of 151 core studies. These studies have been systematically analyzed and evaluated using a well-defined set of evaluation criteria. It is structured around six thematic axes: trends, tasks, techniques, resources, challenges, and ethical concerns, each formulated as a distinct research question. This article also develops several taxonomies and classifications, providing a structured framework for researchers and practitioners to navigate the complexities of applying AI in Qur’anic research. The first taxonomy, a generic taxonomy, highlights key tasks, approaches, modalities, resources, subjects, and languages, offering a comprehensive overview of the field. Another classification focuses on the AI techniques applied in this domain, including machine/deep learning, NLP, speech recognition, computer vision, and ontology-, rule-, and semantic-based approaches. A further taxonomy is developed to address the challenges in this field, categorizing them into Qur’anic-related, computational processing, Arabic NLP-related, limitations of resources, and ethical and religious considerations. It also provides a critical analysis of current approaches in the field, identifies key limitations, and recommends future research directions to enhance progress and address existing challenges. Ultimately, this research serves as a thorough guide, deepening the understanding of the AI landscape in the field and offering valuable insights for developing reliable, advanced, and sensitive AI techniques.

papers.title: Mind perception of artificial intelligence: A systematic review
papers.authors: Li Y., Qin X., Yam K.C., Gray K., Cheng X., Wen J., Lai X.
papers.abstract: Mind perception shapes human-AI interaction, yet there is a lack of comprehensive review for understanding the antecedents and outcomes of the mind perception of AI. This review analyzes 153 empirical studies from the past 20 years and synthesizes the key antecedents and outcomes of the mind perception of AI. We first identify human-related antecedents (e.g., demographics, personality traits, psychological conditions), AI-related factors (e.g., humanlike appearance, transparency, social identity cues, functions), and interaction-related factors (e.g., how humans interact with AI, how AI responds, interaction outcomes) that shape perceptions of AI’s agency and experience. These perceptions of AI’s agency and experience lead to cognitive, emotional, attitudinal, and behavioral consequences that are different from human-human interactions. By comparing findings across the dimensions of agency and experience, we offer nuanced insights into how people perceive AI’s mind and how these perceptions affect human-AI interactions. papers.title: PAGSL: Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning for explainable scholar recommendation

PAGSL combines representation learning and semantic path knowledge to ensure recommendation performance while providing interpretable results from two perspectives. Specifically, it activates latent academic paths among entities through graph augmentation and employs a path-based neural network to encode these paths for recommendation. A masking mechanism with path score optimization is designed to generate concise and informative explanations. We evaluate PAGSL on three academic datasets (Scholat, AMiner, and ResearchGate), comprising approximately 49,000 authors and over 330,000 interaction records. Experimental evaluations validate that PAGSL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving significant improvements of 6.31% in F1-score, 6.29% in Accuracy and 5.95% in AUC for recommendation. Crucially, in terms of explainability, we provide quantitative results and visualization effects. Furthermore, ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our heterogeneous convolution and path representation learning. Domain-specific analysis reveals LLaMA 3.1-405B achieves record Calculus performance (0.717), while DeepSeek-R1 sets unprecedented standards for reasoning transparency (0.716 step-accuracy). Qwen3 models demonstrate exceptional consistency, with mean per-evaluation standard deviation of 0.013, the lowest among Nebius models. Meanwhile, through theoretical analysis of a generated random graph, we derive a lower bound on the approximation quality of the proposed algorithms for recovering ADB structures. Extensive experiments on synthetic bipartite graphs demonstrate the effectiveness and adaptivity of the proposed methods, achieving improvements of up to 39.3% on Jaccard similarity over the state-of-the-art methods.
