papers.title: Hypergraph Kolmogorov–Arnold networks contrastive hashing for unsupervised cross-modal retrieval
papers.authors: Yang Z., Wang B., Long W., Chen Y.
papers.abstract: Cross-modal hashing has become a prominent research focus due to its ability to achieve efficient information retrieval, high-speed query performance, and minimal storage overhead, making it indispensable for processing complex multimedia datasets in academic and industrial applications. However, existing methods suffer from three intertwined challenges: limited nonlinear fitting capacity due to fixed-architecture networks (e.g., MLPs), which struggle to model complex cross-modal semantics; inability to capture beyond-pairwise correlations as they often rely on simple graphs, thus failing to preserve fine-grained structural information; and sensitivity to false-negative pairs in unsupervised contrastive learning, which severely degrades retrieval accuracy. To systematically tackle these challenges, we propose Hyper-KAN Contrastive Hashing (HKCH), an unsupervised framework that introduces three key architectural innovations: first, we redesign the feature mapping module by replacing traditional MLPs with Fast-Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (F-KANs) employing learnable spline-RBF activation functions, enabling dynamic and expressive nonlinear semantic representation; second, we incorporate hypergraph neural networks to model higher-order associations within and across modalities, effectively capturing multi-way structural correlations while filtering semantic redundancy; third, we develop a novel contrastive hashing module with adaptive weights and an improved ternary loss to robustly mitigate false-negative interference and enhance semantic alignment. These components are not merely combined but are structurally integrated into a coherent architecture that advances beyond existing approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that HKCH achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art baselines, with average accuracy gains of 1.38% on MIRFlickr, 1.72% on NUS-WIDE, and 1.37% on MSCOCO significant margins that validate its architectural effectiveness.

papers.title: DiPaNet: Discriminative Pattern-aware Network for Multivariate Time Series Classification
papers.authors: Xiao Z., Hu J., Luo C., Chen X., Wang Y.
papers.abstract: The core objective of multivariate time series classification is to identify temporal-wise and variable-wise discriminative patterns. Previous methods either focus solely on temporal features within individual variables or have limited capacity to model interactions among variables, particularly when capturing short-term patterns (locality) and delayed responses among variables (asynchrony). To address these limitations, we propose a novel method, Discriminative Pattern-aware Network for Multivariate Time Series Classification (DiPaNet), which jointly models discriminative patterns along both the temporal and variable dimensions. Along the temporal dimension, the multivariate time series is divided into local segments, and a temporal convolutional structure is employed to extract temporal-wise discriminative patterns. Along the variable dimension, a Variable Interaction Pattern Detection Module is introduced to capture variable-wise discriminative patterns. In this module, the graph construction step represents each variable within a segment as a node in a graph. The Pattern-based Graph Neural Network incorporates the pattern-based adjacency matrices into the message-passing process and employs pattern fusion to combine node features derived from different patterns, thereby enhancing the model’s sensitivity to critical interaction structures. Experiments on 22 UEA datasets demonstrate that DiPaNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, achieving an average accuracy improvement of 1.8%.

papers.title: Forecasting secondary risks in emergencies: A transferable early warning framework using event logic graphs from social media
papers.authors: Li S., Tian C., Du X., Li Y.
papers.abstract: Social media has become a critical arena for public opinion during emergencies, where the rapid evolution of events can generate unforeseen secondary risks. This study develops and validates a transferable early warning framework that applies Event Logic Graphs (ELGs) to move beyond retrospective analysis, toward proactive risk forecasting. First, this study proposes a novel hybrid Rule-Large Language Model framework to extract events and multiple types of logical relations from noisy social media data. Second, a comparative analysis is conducted by constructing separate ELGs for each event: a natural disaster and public health crisis. Finally, regarding the historical ELG as the knowledge base, the framework incorporates the event chain similarity calculations with context-aware filtering and sentiment enhanced re-ranking mechanism. Specifically, this mechanism ensures prediction validity by filtering context mismatched risks and capturing verified public sentiment to prioritize potential threats. The results present that the hybrid framework significantly outperforms the pure rule-based model in logic triples extraction. The analysis reveals that emergencies evolve into two different structural prototypes: natural disaster is manifested as “linear cascade” models, and public health crisis shows “cyclic feedback loop” characteristics, which provides a new computational perspective for agenda setting theory. In addition, the cross-event secondary risk prediction framework achieves satisfactory predictive performance across Top-3, 5, and 10 cutoffs, demonstrating that integrating context constraints and, more critically, credibility weighted sentiment analysis, achieves the most substantial improvement in identifying high-priority risks. This research contributes to the literature by proposing a robust method for building ELG with multiple logical relationships, helping emergency management shift from passive monitoring to active risk prevention and control.

papers.title: Opinion importance analysis with single-review representation for enhanced restaurant selection decision-making
papers.authors: Chen Z., Chai N., Liang R., Deng M., Wang X., Wang J.
papers.abstract: Online restaurant reviews often express multiple viewpoints within a single review, yet existing studies predominantly focus on aggregated representations at the restaurant level and rarely model the relative importance of opinions at the single-review level. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel opinion importance analysis model that jointly considers content semantics and sentiment characteristics to estimate the relative importance of viewpoints expressed within a single review. Building on this, we develop a single-review level opinion representation framework, together with an opinion completion strategy that infers missing viewpoints based on neighboring reviews, and an importance-aware aggregation mechanism for integrating information across reviews. Experiments on a real-world Yelp dataset comprising 31,412 reviews from 10 restaurants extract six key themes using a combined topic model. Empirical analysis shows that multi-theme opinion expression within individual reviews is prevalent, with approximately 56%–86% of reviews containing viewpoints across multiple themes, while a substantial portion of theme-level opinions remains unobserved within individual reviews. The proposed opinion completion strategy effectively recovers these missing viewpoints, enabling more comprehensive review representations. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that explicitly modeling opinion importance and completing missing viewpoints yield more informative review representations than existing alternatives. Sensitivity analysis further confirms the robustness of the proposed framework with respect to key parameters. This work provides a novel paradigm for review analysis, shifting from coarse-grained aggregation at the restaurant level to fine-grained, single-review opinion modeling that captures both opinion importance and missing viewpoints, with important implications for advanced opinion mining and personalized recommendation systems.

papers.title: CyVerACT: An Agentic Cypher Translation Workflow over Knowledge Graphs
papers.authors: Androna C.M., Mandilara I., Arkadopoulou E., Fotopoulou E., Zafeiropoulos A., Papavassiliou S.
papers.abstract: Question Answering (QA) over Knowledge Graphs (KGs) has greatly benefited from the rapid growth of Large Language Models (LLMs), which enable the translation of natural language questions into Cypher queries. Most existing approaches rely on one-shot generation via in-context learning or on fine-tuning LLMs; however, both strategies often struggle to generate accurate or executable queries, particularly when dealing with complex or unfamiliar graph schemas. To address these limitations, in this work we propose CyVerACT, an agentic workflow for Text-to-Cypher generation that empowers LLMs with execution- and schema-aware feedback mechanisms. CyVerACT leverages CyVer, a software tool that evaluates Cypher queries in terms of syntax validity and semantic compliance with respect to a specific KG schema, and detects their points of failure. The system customizes the input graph schema based on the input question and iteratively refines the generated queries taking advantage of the error metadata from CyVer to guide subsequent LLM generations. We evaluated and compared CyVerACT to existing single-shot generation and iterative refinement approaches in two publicly available Text-to-Cypher datasets of 2180 entries across various domains and complexities, using both foundational (e.g., GPT-4o, LLama-3) and fine-tuned state-of-the-art models. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed workflow significantly improves query correctness and execution success rates, achieving up to 52.7% gain in accuracy in terms of syntax validity and schema access, and 13.5% gain in exact match.

papers.title: Disentangled graph recommendation via dynamic long and short-term intent modeling
papers.authors: Wang J., Wang J., Jin D.
papers.abstract: User decision-making behavior is driven by multiple latent intents. These intents not only reflect user preferences but are also jointly influenced by long-term interests and short-term demands. However, in real-world scenarios, user intents evolve with changes in both time and environment. Existing disentanglement recommendation methods neglect the dynamic characteristic, making it difficult to effectively model the time-varying nature of user intent. Thus, we propose a disentanglement graph recommendation model based on long and short-term intent modeling(DGRLS), aiming to cope with the challenge of dynamic intent modeling. Specifically, DGRLS models user preferences across two dimensions: i) For short-term modeling, dynamic intent routing mechanism is introduced to capture the hierarchical relationships among multi-intent features and to optimize immediate intent through a decay time factor mechanism. ii) For long-term modeling, DGRLS analyzes users’ historical behavioral data employing a large language model, and integrated with a transformer architecture to accurately represent long-term interests. It is worth mentioning that, unlike existing approaches that employ hypergraphs or transformer to model long-term user behavioral preferences, DGRLS models the distribution of users’ dynamic intentions based on modal information in the semantic space. Extensive experiments on three public datasets show that the method is effective, which provides a new perspective for actively understanding modal information for user intent representation.

papers.title: MFC4POI: Multi-factor collaboration for next point-of-interest recommendation using large language models
papers.authors: Song Y., Xu W., Liu L., Tiwari P., Tian G., Xie Q., Peng M.
papers.abstract: Next point-of-interest (POI) recommendation aims to predict the next location a user will visit based on historical behavioral data. Given their strong natural language understanding and reasoning capabilities, large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly introduced into next POI recommendation, as conventional methods are limited by their numerical representations, which often obscure the inherent semantic information embedded in contextual features However, LLM-based approaches struggle to effectively comprehend multiple factors holistically and express them in natural language. To address this issue, we propose Multi-Factor Collaboration for Next POI Recommendation (MFC4POI), a pretraining and fine-tuning framework that reformulates the next POI recommendation task as a question-answering problem. It leverages the strong comprehension and reasoning capabilities of LLMs to analyze user’s current behavior based on historical trajectories, and real time on-site situation, including the dynamic preferences and nearby geographic information in natural language. Due to the inherent limitations of LLMs in accurately modeling temporal and geographical information, MFC4POI introduces an intent identification agent to capture users’ dynamic preferences based on Spatio-temporal Intent-based Knowledge Graph (STIKG). It alleviates the weak spatial reasoning capability of LLMs while providing clear reasoning paths that make the recommendations more intuitive and coherent. To further improve understanding of users’s real-time on-site situation, MFC4POI integrates geographic information with dynamic preferences by providing nearby POIs that align with these dynamic preferences, thereby further enhancing LLMs’ performance. Experiments on three real-world datasets, containing up to 4000 users and 405000 check-ins, show that MFC4POI consistently outperforms strong baselines. Specifically, it achieves better performance than most baselines on Acc@1 and surpasses all baselines on Acc@5 and Acc@10 across all datasets.

papers.title: Adaptive model selection and ensemble via spatiotemporal graph-guided expert routing
papers.authors: Wang L., Cheng S., Lu F.
papers.abstract: Ensemble learning has shown strong potential for spatiotemporal inference by integrating multiple base models to improve accuracy and robustness. However, existing methods often rely on fixed sets of base models and localized ensemble strategies, limiting their adaptability to dynamic data patterns and global spatiotemporal correlations. To address this, we propose an adaptive ensemble framework that dynamically selects and fuses multiple models under varied spatiotemporal conditions. First, a graph-based module is presented to encode the spatial relationships among sensor nodes and the temporal dynamics of their time series into unified context embeddings. Second, an adaptive routing mechanism is designed to compute context-dependent response scores to guide model selection. Finally, a context-specific ensemble strategy aggregates model outputs using weights derived from these scores. Experiments on traffic flow, traffic speed, and air quality datasets show that the proposed framework achieves consistently competitive and often better performance than both mainstream ensemble methods and recent dynamic graph models, reducing inference errors by up to 2.1%-4.7% while using 11%-60% fewer parameters and maintaining comparable inference efficiency. Further interpretability analysis confirms that the framework effectively captures spatiotemporal correlations and performance heterogeneity, thereby enabling adaptive model selection and fusion in response to local contextual variations.

papers.title: Graph-driven knowledge stream method for knowledge management in vertical domain large language models: Case study on pit engineering application
papers.authors: Xia Z., Zhong B., Zhang S., Zhao T.
papers.abstract: Embedding professional knowledge is crucial during developing vertical domain large language models (LLMs). While rapid progress of LLM coexists with barriers to professional knowledge access. Such coexistence highlights the need for effective knowledge management during vertical domain LLM development, yet existing research seldom focuses on this. To solve this gap, we conduct three works: (1) Based on insights of knowledge structural representation, we propose a graph-driven knowledge stream method that models knowledge enabling activities as measurable flows; (2) a knowledge graph (KG)-anchored evaluation protocol is proposed to quantify graph coverage, constraint consistency, hallucination rate, and retention for evaluating knowledge enablement; (3) we integrate graph-anchored evaluation, LLM-graph interaction pipeline, federated learning (FL), and blockchain as graph-driven vertical domain LLM development framework (GVLDF). GVLDF enables knowledge aggregation and reuse, efficacy auditing, and continual optimization. In a foundation pit engineering case study (58,451 tokens fine-tuned vertical domain LLM), GVLDF improved graph coverage from 0.712 to 0.889, raised constraint consistency from 94.3% to 98.1%, and reduced hallucination rate from 0.220 to 0.063, while maintaining retention above 0.87. These findings show that structural anchoring systematically enhances reliability, compliance, and sustainability in vertical LLM development. Our research provides a reliable theory and solution for sustainable enablement and robust deployment of vertical domain LLM.

papers.title: H-ProtoRAG: A hierarchical prototype-based retrieval-augmented framework for multilingual CPC patent classification and prior-art retrieval
papers.authors: Elmi Z.
papers.abstract: Patent documents are long, multi-label, and hierarchically structured texts, which makes joint Cooperative Patent Classification (CPC) assignment and prior-art retrieval particularly challenging in multilingual settings. Existing patent classifiers and retrievers typically treat sections and tasks in isolation and often under-specify how retrieved evidence should influence final label decisions and calibration. We propose H-ProtoRAG, a hierarchical prototype-based, retrieval-augmented framework that couples dual encoders with section-aware pooling over titles, abstracts, and claims, a claim–evidence alignment module trained on PatentMatch, and a multi-loss objective combining cross-entropy, supervised contrastive, prototype, hierarchical, retrieval, and NLI terms. For claim–evidence supervision, we adopt a fixed multilingual NLI teacher, namely XLM-R fine-tuned on XNLI, as the default pseudo-labeling mechanism; token-overlap rules are retained only as a lexical ablation to quantify the gap between surface-form heuristics and semantically grounded pseudo-labeling. Using 1.2M Turkish/English patents from the BigQuery CPC corpus together with BIGPATENT, PatentMatch, CLEF-IP 2010, MAREC, and PatTR, we evaluate H-ProtoRAG under in-domain, cross-source, and multilingual scenarios. On Turkish CPC classification, H-ProtoRAG improves Micro-F1 from 45.3% (PatentBERT) to 55.3% and Hierarchical-F1 from 55.0% to 63.7%; on English, it raises Micro-F1 from 52.0–53.8% to 58.6%. On CLEF-IP 2010 prior-art retrieval, our hybrid dense–sparse retriever with cross-encoder re-ranking increases nDCG@10 from 0.212 (BM25) to 0.301 and Precision@1 from 0.41 to 0.60 while maintaining Recall@50 at 69.4%. The same retrieval stack is further used to construct teacher-supervised evidence signals that recalibrate classification scores under hierarchical CPC ambiguity. Calibration is also improved, with Expected Calibration Error reduced from 12.4% to 6.1% and top-5% prediction precision increased from 71% to 85%, supporting more reliable multilingual patent analytics.

papers.title: LLM-assisted fake news detection with adaptive boosting framework incorporating contrastive learning
papers.authors: Yin S., Wang Y., Hou D., An W., Gao C., Li X., Wang Z.
papers.abstract: With the rapid development of digital technologies, the widespread spread of fake news on social media platforms may threaten social stability. Existing methods often use small models as feature extractors for news content, relying on the inherent pattern differences between true and false news as the basis for fake news detection. However, smaller models cannot perceive latent background information in news content. Additionally, fake news is much less prevalent than true news on real social platforms, which may lead to issues with data collection imbalance of true and false labels. These challenges may limit the effectiveness of existing detection methods. Therefore, we propose a Large Language Model-assisted Fake News Detection method with Adaptive Boosting, denoted as LFND-AB. Specifically, we first employ the large language model to generate analyses of the truthfulness and falseness of news text, which contains background information about the news. We then design an explainable base learner for fake news detection that utilizes contrastive learning to align the similarity between the news text and the corresponding generated analyses to obtain higher-quality fused representations. Furthermore, we design an adaptive ensemble boosting framework based on the base learner. This framework adjusts the weights of misclassified samples to improve the detection performance in the next base learner, thereby optimizing the model’s ability to handle label imbalance. The comprehensive experiments conducted on benchmark datasets demonstrate that both the proposed base learner and LFND-AB outperform State-Of-The-Art (SOTA) methods. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/cgao-comp/FEND.

papers.title: R&D partner recommendation and network prediction using patent data: A deep learning approach
papers.authors: Wang J., Chen H.W., Shih Y.H.
papers.abstract: R&D partner selection is often guided by expert judgment, and prior patent-based studies rarely integrate bibliometric, semantic, and network evidence in a unified predictive framework. This study develops a deep learning approach that fuses patent bibliometric indicators, SBERT-based textual embeddings, and network link prediction features to recommend R&D partners and anticipate future collaboration networks. Using USPTO patent applications in the self-driving vehicle domain (2018 to 2023), we construct a dataset of 23,796 patents, including 5237 collaborative patents. The fused model achieves 83.33% precision, 66.67% F1, and 57.55% PR-AUC, improving F1 and PR-AUC by 3.18 and 5.18 percentage points over the strongest single-feature baseline. It also outperforms classical machine-learning baselines, raising PR-AUC by 20.58 percentage points relative to XGBoost. SHAP-based analysis indicates complementary contributions from bibliometric, semantic-textual, and network signals, supporting shortlists for both exploitation-oriented and exploration-oriented collaboration strategies. Beyond partner recommendations, the model offers forward-looking insights into network evolution, indicating a continued tendency toward denser and more interconnected collaboration clusters in this sector.

papers.title: An All-in-One Quality Assessment Agent for 4D digital human: Bridging talking heads and animated human
papers.authors: Zhou Y., Zhang Z., Wen F., Xu L., Zhang Y., Zhou Y., Cao J., Shi Y., Liu X., Min X., Wang Y., Zhai G.
papers.abstract: As advancements in 4D digital human (4DDH) technology continue to progress rapidly, ensuring and evaluating its quality has become a significant concern. To support the ongoing development of 4DDH and enhance user experience, we conduct a comprehensive quality assessment of 4DDH content. Specifically, we introduce H4DQA, the large-scale 4DDH quality assessment dataset, comprising 3220 4DDH samples categorized into two groups: Talking Head and Animated Human. Furthermore, the dataset incorporates model-based, motion-based, and quality of experience (QoE) distortions to enhance diversity and robustness in quality assessment. Building upon the H4DQA dataset, we develop an All-in-One Quality Assessment Agent (A3gent) for 4DDHs, leveraging a multimodal large language model (MLLM). This framework provides an effective, reliable, and efficient objective quality assessment method for 4DDHs. The proposed A3gent integrates visual, phonetic, and posture features, achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on the H4DQA dataset. Our approach offers valuable insights for advancing digital human technology and establishing standardized quality assessment protocols.
